This game got insanely negative reviews when it first came out, but the devs have improved it so much - it definitely does not deserve those reviews now.
A lot of the Federation missions are inspired by the Deep Space 9 and Voyager TV series and work great in the game.
The game starts you out as a Federation / Klingon / Romulan officer and your goal is to complete missions and work your way up through the ranks till you become a respected Admiral / General. For each mission you complete you get credits and exp, which is typical in an MMO-RPG. You can also gain "Dilithium" which is a rarer currency used to buy special upgrades for your ship, or can be exchanged into "Zen" (the game's premium currency) via an exchange.
Every 10 levels you have access to a new ship for free, but once you hit levels 50/60 (max level), you will need to buy your ships with either an insane amount of credits or Zen. Weapons and ship parts can be found as drops from enemies, or can be bought from the credit exchange (usually pretty cheaply, depending on the level and rarity).
I do have a problem with this game and that is that a lot of the endgame content is very hard to get without dipping your hand into your wallet. Say you want to buy a ship for 2000-2500 Zen (the typical price) - that'll set you back about 25 euros. You found the same ship on the credit exchange for 90 million? Well, to be able to get more than 10 million credits you'll need to unlock your account credit limit for 500 Zen (about 5 euros)... Of course you could save up your Dilithium, but to buy a ship we're talking nearly 600-700K (depends on how ridiculous the DIL-ZEN exchange ratio is), which will take you weeks to farm.
All-in-all, I loved the time I spent on this game and I would recommend it to any MMO-RPG and/or Trek fan - just beware the pay-wall once you hit levels 50-60.

This game is, well, dicey to recommend. On one hand, it's probably one of the best PC games I own in my personal taste. But on the other hand, it's one of the most subjective and 'iffy' games out there.
For starters, if you want to make a new account, you best be ready to hassle EA's help division to no end. Be it phone calls, or instant chatting, get someone from inside the company to help you with it, specifically if you buy from Steam. The game also has registry errors if you happen to be the happy owner of Windows 7 64-bit. Overall, it's a lot of hassle that may make the game not worth it, just to get it running. It will leave a sour taste in your mouth that, for some, will absolutely spoil the experience.
But nobody ever dug up gold without effort.
And that's what this game is. Creative gold. This game, especially if you purchase it with the Galactic Adventures pack essentially is one of the most massive, creative sandbox experiences you'll see ANYWHERE. It avoids the issues games like Gmod have by restricting you in a way, but it simultaneously allows you to run wild in a strange mix between progression and restriction. A strange mix that feels rewarding and meaningful, as a player.
Taken on their own, each stage is fairly bland(outside of space). You've got your cell stage, basically a 2D space game. Your creature stage, which if you play offensively is like a stripped down MMO, or if you play socially like a poor clone of The Sims. And finally, you've got a couple of RTS stages where you conquer other groups/nations.
However, it seems as though the game developers knew that none of these were particularly fantastic, because none of them really overstay their welcome, and they all build up the skills you need to take on the Space Stage.
In the Space Stage, you play an intergalactic ambassador/emperor of sorts. Establish trade routes with other sentient races, declare war on your enemies and steal their planets, colonize and expand into a galactic empire, singlehandedly battle space fleets, beam down to planets in Star-Trek-Episode-esque segments(if you have galactic adventures), and battle an incredible army of increasingly deadly cyborgs to reach the center of the galaxy. All while playing as a creature of YOUR design, flying a ship that YOU created.
And in the back of your mind, always remember that you started this journey as a tiny, single-celled organism.
So, yes. This game is sheer gold. However, it is not without its problems. Between having to hassle with EA's tech support(of all things) and fixing potential registry errors, you have a lot on your plate if you want to play this game. But if you ever find it on sale, buy it. Just shut up and do it. It may be a pain at first, but chances are, if you like the idea of being an intergalactic god or goddess in a nearly infinite sandbox, this is the game for you.

If you're gonna get it, get it while it's 5 bucks. That is the price it is really worth, maybe 6. This game is a good stepping-stone for the evolution genre, and a few other indie games are following in it's path if you dig around on the internet. It's the first iteration of a still new genre. You can create a variety of your own creatures in the brilliant creature creator, and the main appeal of this is being able to see other people's creations in your world! Cool right?
Well EA has abandoned this game, so don't expect to see anything cool other than what the game developers put in there. Sometimes you can see your own creations, so that's cool.
Unfortunately, despite the variety of creatures, most of them behave the same way. You a few abilities, ranging from stealth to very limited flying. You can be a herbivore, omnivore, or carnivore.
The game has 5 stages that are all pretty different, but the game shines in Creature mode, the second stage. Where you control one creature in your species, and evolve it as it gets more sentient. Like I said before, most creatures behave the same way in Creature mode. They all hang around in their nests and hardly interact with eachother, and if they do they don't do it enough. I wanted to see creatures huntings other creatures, and bird-like creatures and bugs, but all I saw was one wandering into an aggressive territory and getting slaughtered. There is no variety of roles in the ecosystem of the game. It's just "Five Boogleborfs hanging around a nest. Kill them or sing at them?" And that's it.
Sometimes you see "Epics" which are huge creatures, that are indeed epic. Every once in a while a world event happens, like a meteor shower or a UFO flies by. While cool, they don't mean anything.
They did a good job of making a world that looks real from far away. But get closer, and you see all sorts of flaws and places for massive improvement.
Buy it now while it's 5 bucks. Otherwise I don't recommend. Stick around, in a while "THRIVE" will come out. Look it up, it sounds good.
EDIT: It's good for kids though. I got this game when I was a little naive to the world of gaming, that's where most of my playtime come from.

Full review:
Metal Slug 3, originally released on the Neo-Geo, has now been ported to Steam. I've never played a Metal Slug game before, so I was eager to find out why they were so loved.
I'll start by saying that this game is hard. Like, ridiculously hard. I managed to complete the first four levels on medium, but I wasn't able to pass the final level on medium. After six or so tries (getting 30-40 minutes into the level each time) I gave up and switched to easy, which I was able to pass with 13 credits remaining, surprisingly. It was frustrating, but the feeling of relief after beating that last level was enough for me to forget my frustration.
The game is very short, lasting about two hours (or three, if you're terrible at it, like me), but it was an experience well had. This was my introduction to the world of Metal Slug, and I quite enjoyed it. The gameplay was, for the most part, fun and kept me playing (until the final mission, where I rage quit three separate times) till the end. The gameplay doesn't consist of much, just your average sidescroller with plenty of weapons (too many to name), but the game's humor and variety really made it an enjoyable experience for me.
This didn't come without its issues, however. The game, being originally for the Neo-Geo, was running through some sort of emulator, and it did quite a bad job at its sole task. Putting the game's resolution at anything other than the default (I played at 1920x1080) results in constant frame drops. The actual fps of the game remains the same (60fps), but the emulation appears to slow down considerably. This really messed with me during the final mission, where I experienced the issue the most. That alone caused quite a few rage quits during my play session with the game.
On top of the fps issues, the game also appears to have some sound issues. Sometimes, a noticeable increase/decrease in the sound speed can be heard. This is often heard in the game's music, which I found quite annoying. It doesn't happen too often, but it does enough for me to point it out.
Regardless of the game's flaws, Metal Slug 3 does a fantastic job of retaining its fun factor from the original release. The included co-op mode is also a bonus, although I wasn't able to try it out myself. I can recommend the game, but beware of the technical flaws that are included.

To be honest... I've been anticipating this game for a while now. And now that that I got my hands on it, sat down to play it a while and even got together with a friend of mine for a session. The problems we encountered however, was clearly apparent. Whether it was either a laggy connection on my end or graphical lag on his end, neither of us could figure out what was going on. Even when I played this on single player and even turned the video settings down as low as they could go, I was still dealing with a major delay issue. Another issue I have is that you only have 20 continues. It feels a bit limiting, but considering the fact that this was replicating the same feel of the arcade classic, I feel that's only a minor gripe. The controls also feel kinda wonky for keyboard users too, but again. Small potatoes.
But onto the positives! For one thing, the classic feel of running and gunning while - attempting to, anyway - dodging as much traffic as this game can throw at you and HOLY BALLS does this game deal out punishment for slackers and those who get too cocky in spades. But then again, this is what makes this game fun. Sure, it's frustrating as all hell, but that's the beauty part of it! It keeps you coming back for more with each and every level you progress, every mook you bring down, every boss battle you win, every time you get killed, pretty much everything about this game makes you want to keep pushing forward. It's that drive, you know? Something you'll never get from modern games of today. But hey, that's just me. But overall, I have a mixed opinion about this port of Metal Slug 3, but I would still recommend this, given there's a few glaring issues I have with this. And on top of that, at this price? I'd say it's worth it!

I played the original Panzer Elite upon release and even purchased the re-release as there are not many Tank Simulation games.
This Panzer Elite Action Gold Edition is not a Tank Simulation game either.
The game play here is exceedingly simple. You drive along, you shoot at the enemy in a very arcade style manner.
The voice acting is not bad, and there's an attempt to make you feel you are part of a tank crew.
The main, and unforgivable problem, is the physics are absurd. Your tank can't go up an incline, you will roll over your tank so often, the game actually has built in code to flip your tank back upright automatically. You aren't rolling your tank because you approached an angle incorrectly, but because you turned on flat ground too fast and rolled your tank over. Your squad will also accidentally ram your tank and flip you over.
You can run over any tree in existence and barely slow down, but you can't travese the smallest of steps.
I finally had to stop "playing" to see if it could get any better, when my force of tanks was spread out and we were being attacked (as usual) by overwhelming numbers of enemy tanks (that never do anything other than drive straight toward you, then turn to create rear kill shots) and one the tanks in my group clipped me, that bounced me into another one of my units tanks, which bounced me into another one of my units tanks, which bounced me into another tank, and because I'm not driving forward, all the tanks stop, so my command tank is literally bouncing around like a pinball off of one tank to another tank, while spinning like a made top.

Panzer Elite Action Gold Edition, the one you will actually get, is a totally different game from Panzer Elite, the one you are able to see on the store page. (For example, track in screenshot seems able to move but become just a pair of fixed blocks in the game.
The shortage of this game which I found had already been written in comments by others so I am not going to repeat them again.
If Panzer Elite is a game between good and fair, in my opinion, Panzer Elite Action Gold Edition would be bad for sure.

After the awesome that was Panzer Elite, the addition of the work "Action" to the title is a sad step backwards.
The missions are very linear and very repetitive, with no opportunity for long range spotting or gunnery for the most part or room to maneuver, but it doesn't matter.  The enemy AI will blindly and foolishly charge you with a suicidal enthusiasm and their tanks never seem to be a match for yours.
All the cool penetration and damage mechanics are gone, replaced by a simple hit point style system.
There is no system for modifying your vehicles and repairs and rearming are arcade-ish.
If you want a light game that requires no thought and happens to feature armor this might be good for a few hours of distraction.  If you are looking for something like the original Panzer Elite, you might consider something more along the lines of T34 vs. Tiger.

Morrowind is thee absolute best game ever made. The grand scope of this game changed gaming and my life forever. When it was released back in 2002 there was nothing quite like it. Not even close. I was initialy drawn to the game when I was  14 in around 2004  because it had first person as well as third person gameplay. I had never seen a first person aspect in a sword and sorcery rpg type world. I wasnt really into rpgs because of the game mechanics, I hated seeing xp subtracted on someones head everytime I hit them. just broke the immersion for me. Which was a shame because I loved the subject matter of rpgs. Once I sank my teeth in and realized how immense the scale of this world was, I was hooked, and hooked forever. Sure the textures and graphics are a bit dated, but that can be remedied now with the Morrwind Overhaul. There are alot of new comers to the world of Tamriel, millions infact. Especially after the huge success of Oblivion & Skyrim. Morrowind was and still is considered more of a "nerdy rpg" mostly because the conversations are text and the old rpg style combat system where you would miss alot if your skill wasnt high enough with that  particular weapon calss. In my opinion, text conversations is alot faster than having to wait for the NPC to finish with their slow paced dialogue which is normally just as long( word wise). Don't get me wrong, I loove Oblivion, and I LOOOVE Skyrim, but over the years they have done alot more hand holding for younger generations of gamers. In Morrowind you had to use your map, journal, clues, and brain to find out what you had to do. You had to ask questions, there were no map markers,  and there was no fast travel other than Silt Striders. That is what made Morrowind seem so alive, you were dropped in an alien world and you had to figure things out for yourself including the rules. I remember my first playthrough, I went into the first shop with a tavern on the second story. I looked at a table and saw a sword and I remember thinking "Eh, I dont think anyone would mind if I take this.." I took it and the next thing I heard was swords unsheathing and saw a giant ball of electricity hit me and kill me instanty. Thats when I learned to save often, Vvardenfell is a dangerous place. You had to live and learn, and try again. I dont even think I knew what the word "barter" meant back then to be honest, but boy did I learn it and learn it well. Anyone who talks down on Morrowind in any way obviously still wets the bed.   This game is your grandfather, and you will show him some respect. If you are a true Elder Scrolls fan and want to see where it all came from, then you have quite the adventure waiting for you. If you are Uber TES fan then I would suggest getting daggerfall from the elderscrollswiki its free and has an automated DOSbox setup for all new versions of windows 7,8.1 etc. However, If you're a SNOT-NOSED GUMSHOE, who doesn't respect history or where things came from, then don't let the chitin door hit you in the butt. Toukiden 2 a monster-slaying action RPG set in an open-world, fantasy medieval Japan.
Pros:
- A huge selection of weapon types and equipment sets, enabling a wide range of play styles, including melee combat with swords, spears, clubs, etc or ranged combat with bows and guns.
- Beautifully designed characters with Japanese voiceovers.
- Fast paced combat, both in ground or air with the new Demon Hand against various Japanese monsters.
- A huge open world with many different vibes to each setting.
- Performance-wise, very smooth.
Cons:
- Character models look lifeless, no mouth animation.
- World models look outdated.
- Story is somewhat weak compared to other JRPGs.

At first, i must say that i'm playing this game with my gamepad (Xbox, Thrustmaster GPX lightback), which works just great, but if you don't have gamepad or you just don't like to play on it, you will not be happy with Toukiden 2.
This is just awesome "monster hunting" game. While Kiwami was more like MH clone with different setting and combat mechanics, Toukiden 2 feels more like mix of Kiwami, Way of the Samurai and sometimes i just feel some Dragon's Dogma flow.
Open World is great improvement, you can use portal stones to travel to distant bases (you have to discover 'em first), so you don't have to travel all the way every time. There is a day / night cycle, including tasks which only can be done in certain part of the day. Quest system has been also improved, now you can accept quests from ppl you meet in town or during your travels through open world.
PROS:
Story - very good imo, game is more story-driven than Kiwami.
Gameplay - monster hunting for materials and Mitama, crafting, equipment and Mitama boosting. There are "duty" tasks which leads you through story line, side quests, missions and more :)
Combat - imo much better than in Kiwami, Demon Hand (kind of grappling hook) is great improvement, bonus skills from Mitama as well. Thanks to Demon Hand mechanics, you can finally hit Oni upper parts even with long swords, hit flying Oni or just reach any target very fast. You can choose from 11 different types of weapons, each with it's own style.
Music - well, music is great, but you can hear many same tracks as in Kiwami
Graphics - seems a little bit outdated, but some sceneries looks very good, definitely better than Kiwami.
Voice acting - only Japanese, but really good
CONS:
Subtitles - sometimes you'll find that there are no subtitles for some audio lines, usually when your companions are chatting on the way, so it's nothing gamebreaking, but i'd just rather know what are they talking about .)
Settings - while you can set gfx settings in game main menu, you have to restart the game otherwise some settings as light shafts on/off won't work (so it's better to set it up in settings window before the game starts)
Controls - no mouse support (i never tried it, but that's what most negative reviews says)
Display - it does not support 4k (1920 x 1080 max, 60 fps cap - i don't care about this, but i think it's good to mention it for anyone who cares)
Overall: awesome story-driven monster hunting game, much better than it's predecessor.
For Monster Hunter fans, I'd recommend Toukiden 2 if you'd like something with faster-paced combat and more story/character focus. Just make sure you have a controller.

Toukiden 2. How should I say this?
It is such a great improvement from Kiwami. Seriously.
Considering how bad that port was, this was so much better. I barely had any crashes, and lag just wasn't there. The funny thing is, all those bad reviews when the game first came out was from no mouse and keyboard support. Just buy a controller and play this game if you're a Monster Hunter fan, it's a great substitute for PC. But if you want a Pros and Cons list, here you go.
PROS:
-Graphically pleasing, not the best, but it's still cool.
-Decent story, though a little rushed at times (But that's just me nitpicking)
-A lot of armor sets and weapons (They even added about two more weapon types, sword & shield and chain & whip)
-Characters can be pretty amusing at times, it doesn't feel like they're just robots saying the lines because they were ordered to.
-Voice acting is great too.
-Gameplay is great.
-Game isn't too difficult, or too easy.
-Grammar mistakes at times, but this always gives me a laugh so I'll put it here, in PROs. (This is also me nitpicking)
-Has multiplayer. (Though if you want to play with less than four friends, you'd have to take NPCs with you. But that's it.)
CONS:
-The Multiplayer has a built in mic, which I honestly don't want to use. So far I'm not sure if there's a way to turn off the mic.
-No Keyboard+Mouse support, but honestly, this isn't such a big problem. You can easily just configure your keyboard to your liking, or just buy a controller, which I highly suggest you do.
In conclusion, Toukiden 2 is a great game. Buy it. If you don't think it's worth the price, wait for some sort of a sale. Then buy it.

Pro:

- Lots of ways to customize the game in the options (also your player model)

Neutral:
- It takes a bit to get used to the movement if you aren't a quake pro. Once you got it, it's a lot more fun. (You might need to watch a tutorial video like I did, check this out:

The game can be a bit frustrating in the beginning because of these two things. It won't be like this for a long time though.
Cons:
- Only few players. But there are always enough to play with.
- When you enter a server it'll download the map directly through steam. So when the download is finished and you have another download queued it'll start downloading that stuff. So you have to enter Steam and stop the download everytime. I hope there will be fix soon.
Conclusion:
This isn't a game where you can kill ten people out of a chopper, burn someone with a big cone of fire or slow people until they're frozen. It's a classic arena shooter where you need aiming and movement skills. And if you're good at those you'll get rewarded for it.

The Good
1. It's very easy to pick up, shallow learning curve.

The Bad

The Ugly
So much untapped potential in the game. I'm sure the devs know that too.
Some ideas:
1. Choosing season rules to start with
2. Choosing fuel amounts
3. Driver injury, long term, short term, recovery times.
4. Sponsorship structure needs a rethink.

6. We have a test track? - let's use it!
7. Telemetry data? would be nice to see something telemetry looking like with some options to improve/invest/fix
8. Press events! - you know when all the drivers get to sit, pretend they like it and talk to the media...

10. Driver seat mode! - can we get some watered down driver seat 3D view? (maybe for MM2?)
11. Multiplayer!!! - (definitely MM2 territory)

I could probably extend this to 50 so I'll stop here.
Verdict:
Should you get this game? - yes.

This turned out to be huge fun.
I've never followed F1 or GT motorsports but the game draws the player in kind of like Football Manager does even for someone who knows nothing about "soccer football" <grin>.
It is a management game, not a driving simulation.
It doesn't have any F1 etc licensing so you will not see names or images of famous racing teams, drivers, mechanics, designers, events(?) etc. It is all fictitious except maybe some of the track layouts not sure.
It is a simulation-oriented game and even though I know nothing about motorsports I'd certainly call it "evocative". Maybe the only thing missing from that evocation is the carnival atmosphere you hear about from real-life spectators of the sport.
I enjoy the race strategy. I do see it as a little bit mathematical (for me that is a good thing), you have to figure out the fixed fuel-per-lap burn rates in the game for different engine settings (which takes a few laps of your first race) and balance those against "tyre" wear rates that depend on driver, temperature, track etc.
There are a couple ways I've played this. Aggressive, once your parts have enough reliability, you use the fact that fuel weighs more than the time to add it in the pit stop (the big time consumption of a pit stop is entering and exiting the pit lane) and run high output with just enough fuel levels to cover the time it takes the softest slick to wear down. Or conservative, you use the fact that that pit lane entry and exit time is worth a second of lap time over many laps, so you load up on fuel for the long haul and conserve fuel and "tyre" wear as much as possible to minimise the number of pit stops. You can see there is some balancing to work out here and depending on your team and drivers and car the same strategy may work sometimes and not others.
There are some quirks I've noticed. Some probably intended, some not. I'm going to give a lot of verbage to these because I don't see a lot of discussion about them, but don't let me convey that I don't very much like the game and rate it one my best Steam purchases.
There are some annoying dialog issues that make no sense. Like one that asks you to "bring in" a driver that beat yours, and gets them mad when you refuse, but they happen to already be your other driver. So either answer you♥♥♥♥♥♥off one of your drivers. Not that unavoidable ego issues are not part of the sport (they are a big part of this management sim) but the pretext in this case is absurd. However, okay, that is not huge deal and I'm sure in some future patch it will be handled.
Also, your first set of "tyres" in a race will start at a lower temperature than every other set put on the car at a pit stop. I know nothing, but maybe this is due to the time sitting still on the grid in the starting lane until the lights go out?
The second and subsequent seasons all the cars start with very poor reliability parts, much worse than the first season. To the point where it doesn't seem like the intention of the design. I'd almost expect it to be the other way around. Note that the AI has the same issues here - first races of the season are fraught with mechanical issues for them too.
The part design tool tips state unequivocally you unlock slots on design iterations. This is not actually technically how it works. You only unlock the next slot when you use one of the highest-grade components. That one is really annoying but just because the instructions mess you up a little in a long-term way (the perpetual chase of improving parts design is one of the main game aspects).
Finally I will caution you that the game (at least since the GT patch if not before) has a serious actual bug, however, which I hope the developers will read about and fix.
When the 1st place, or perhaps other, driver is a lap (or laps) ahead of a chasing car, and that chasing car pulls ahead, the game bumps the former-chaser's time by one whole lap all of a sudden (you can see the seconds whiz by on the upper left display). This effectively jumps that car up a lap and in some cases a car which has been lapped can even take the lead this way. Not sure it *always* happens (it is a busy game) but I've seen it 5 or 6 times now and have confirmed what seems to be other plays who have seen it (see link below).

This game is a puzzle game that I found to be incredibly simple. That is coming from somebody who declares himself
bad at puzzle games. There are 24 levels in total which in all took me 65 minutes to complete. I would recommend this puzzle game if you are looking for a puzzle game that isn’t going to take much thought to complete. If you want to relax with a simple puzzle game for roughly an hour, then I’d say this game is for you. But, I feel like that is not what most people are looking to get out of a puzzle game, because of that I’m not going to be recommending this game.
With this review, I’ll be implementing a new system for all puzzle reviews in the future which I’ll be calling
– 3/10 I found this game very simple as previously stated, I would simply lock one square in a safe room and then solve the other “hemisphere” and then take the other square out of the safe room to finish the level. I did that 24 times and beat the game.
– There are none.
– The music is relaxing and something I found myself enjoying. However, I did begin to notice the loops after my short time of playing this game.
– 65 Minutes
– You’ll use A & D to control the squares, and left/right click to change colors. I found these controls semi confusing at times due to the fact that I frequently got mixed up on which way the squares would move when I hit the different directional keys. I suppose that’s the nature of these “Split Hemisphere” types of games though.
– Turning Music on/off and turning sound on/off are your only options in this game. A volume slider would be nice.
– I don’t feel like I was forced to master concepts of the game in order to advance in the game. I feel like I found a tactic (the safe room tactic I previously spoke of) and stuck with it.
– These bugs are definitely easier witnessed in the video than explained, however I’ll try to explain. And you may say, well you went looking for these bugs, and yeah, I did. That’s what I feel a reviewer should do. In total I found two bugs, with one being an actual bug and the other being what I’ll refer to as a hitbox error.
The “Push-out Bug” – This bug is replicated by going inside an “obstacle” for instance a yellow rectangle that can only be passed while the color is set to yellow. Once inside the obstacle if the color is changed to any of the other colors the square that is inside the obstacle is pushed through the obstacle. This allows for players to no clip through an area of a level to make the level easier. Even in some cases it allows the player to enter the entire other hemisphere of the game so that both squares are on the same side.
The Spike Bug – The hitbox on the spikes extends just a tad too far, and if the cube is sliding down the wall where a spike is at the bottom of the wall, in a case where the spike wouldn’t hit you it still kills you. This is hard to explain in text, but it is displayed in the video if you’re interested in seeing what I’m talking about.
My Recommendations: If DahlGames happens to be reading this review, these are my recommendations to make the game better in my opinion. Firstly, fixing the bugs is of utmost importance. Secondly, consider adding another level pack. But in the second level pack, I would recommend designing the levels with half of the colors being used. This will keep players from simply solving the puzzles one hemisphere at a time, and will make the game more difficult.
If my suggestions are used, or changes are made to the game that you feel makes this review unfair, please contact me and I’ll be more than happy to consider redoing this review.

Morrowind is thee absolute best game ever made. The grand scope of this game changed gaming and my life forever. When it was released back in 2002 there was nothing quite like it. Not even close. I was initialy drawn to the game when I was  14 in around 2004  because it had first person as well as third person gameplay. I had never seen a first person aspect in a sword and sorcery rpg type world. I wasnt really into rpgs because of the game mechanics, I hated seeing xp subtracted on someones head everytime I hit them. just broke the immersion for me. Which was a shame because I loved the subject matter of rpgs. Once I sank my teeth in and realized how immense the scale of this world was, I was hooked, and hooked forever. Sure the textures and graphics are a bit dated, but that can be remedied now with the Morrwind Overhaul. There are alot of new comers to the world of Tamriel, millions infact. Especially after the huge success of Oblivion & Skyrim. Morrowind was and still is considered more of a "nerdy rpg" mostly because the conversations are text and the old rpg style combat system where you would miss alot if your skill wasnt high enough with that  particular weapon calss. In my opinion, text conversations is alot faster than having to wait for the NPC to finish with their slow paced dialogue which is normally just as long( word wise). Don't get me wrong, I loove Oblivion, and I LOOOVE Skyrim, but over the years they have done alot more hand holding for younger generations of gamers. In Morrowind you had to use your map, journal, clues, and brain to find out what you had to do. You had to ask questions, there were no map markers,  and there was no fast travel other than Silt Striders. That is what made Morrowind seem so alive, you were dropped in an alien world and you had to figure things out for yourself including the rules. I remember my first playthrough, I went into the first shop with a tavern on the second story. I looked at a table and saw a sword and I remember thinking "Eh, I dont think anyone would mind if I take this.." I took it and the next thing I heard was swords unsheathing and saw a giant ball of electricity hit me and kill me instanty. Thats when I learned to save often, Vvardenfell is a dangerous place. You had to live and learn, and try again. I dont even think I knew what the word "barter" meant back then to be honest, but boy did I learn it and learn it well. Anyone who talks down on Morrowind in any way obviously still wets the bed.   This game is your grandfather, and you will show him some respect. If you are a true Elder Scrolls fan and want to see where it all came from, then you have quite the adventure waiting for you. If you are Uber TES fan then I would suggest getting daggerfall from the elderscrollswiki its free and has an automated DOSbox setup for all new versions of windows 7,8.1 etc. However, If you're a SNOT-NOSED GUMSHOE, who doesn't respect history or where things came from, then don't let the chitin door hit you in the butt. Morrowind is quite possibly my favorite game of all time. It was my introduction to the Elder Scrolls series back on the Xbox, and as such it holds a special place in my heart. Anyone who is a fan of RPG's and hasn't played this game yet should do so immediately. The gameplay is solid, the plot is rich and engrossing, and the world is enormous and almost alien in the way that it looks nothing like what you would expect a fantasy world to look like. Really, that itself is the beauty of the Elder Scrolls games. Bethesda has created a world which draws on the typical fantasy ideas, and then turns them on their heads to create an atmosphere which is completely unique. Where else would you find cannibalistic wood elves, dwarves who aren't really dwarves, or bipedal lizards who worship a race of magical, sentient trees? Only in The Elder Scrolls.
A word of warning, though: for anyone who is used to the gameplay in Oblivion/Skyrim, you may be in for a rude awakening. While the newer Elder Scrolls games have become more "streamlined" and "action-y," Morrowind is an RPG in the truest sense of the word. The most noticeable difference is in the way combat works. In Oblivion/Skyrim, you stand in front of someone, swing your sword, and hit them. In Morrowind, you could be right in front of an enemy and completely miss. This is because Morrowind uses the old-school dice-rolling mechaninc to determine if your attacks are successful or not. Even your spells can fail to cast if you're not proficient enough in that particular school of magic. No, it's not lag. No, the hitboxes are not broken. That's just the way a real RPG works. Things like this can be frustrating to newer players who aren't used to it, which is completely understandable. But for those who persevere and get past this learning curve, you will be treated to one of the most rewarding and memorable gaming experiences ever. You won't be disappointed.

To all those negative reviews saying that Morrowind is much more difficult than the sequels and that it's a huge leap for a modern gamer to take: I agree with you. My first Elder Scrolls was Skyrim, and as Oblivion and Morrowind went on sale I bought those too. Morrowind is my absolute favourite, despite the fact that when I started I was killed by a slaughterfish and a mudcrab.
In Skyrim, and to an extent Oblivion, you start out average and work your way up to being great. In Morrowind you start out terrible, work your way up to average, and them become well-nigh invincible. And the sense of satisfaction that comes with that is absolutely unreal.
Sure the graphics might not be incredible, and the combat might be frustrating, but once you've sunk a few hours into it you won't even notice. And if there's something about the game you don't like, there's a mod for that!
In short form: Get this game, have some patience, give it some time to grow on you, and become a god.

This game is great as one of those you take on a laptop on a train.
If you have ever wanted to create your own racing team and manage most aspects, from driver to development to sponserships then this is likely to be right up your alley.
There is a good amount of depth (I noticed a few reviews saying otherwise), I think it could be deeper but then you would lose some of the enjoyment in my opinion.
There is a bit of repetition and my main criticism of the game is that the practice sessions are too punishing to not take manually each time and when you do take them they start on short time limits in most games.
It would be nice to have much longer (longer than you need even) but the ability to skip into the next session (like F1 2016 for example).
The above is also why it feels like a good game to take on a laptop away as you can dive in , do a race weekend (get your fill of the repetative parts) and then leave it for a period.
The customisation is great as well, creating your own team lets you feel more invested as does making your character at the start (complete with the backstory).
Also the range of starting teams is great. So if you want to just learn to play you can start with a mid range or decvent front runner before starting your own team or taking over one of the very back markers.
I havent had any technical issues even after the DLC and the workshop released it has been reliable every time.
Overall I would recommend this to anyone who likes F1 or motoracing and fancies managing their own team.
Personally £25 is a lot of money but given the normal price of games i would say this is worth it. Plus it seems like there will be more content added and its being worked on and improved.
We already had a 2D mode to make it better for laptop and lower end machines for example.

This is a set that contains both Panzer Elite Action-Fields of Glory and its expansion,Dunes of War. The game isn't too bad and seeing as you get both the game and its expansion there isn't much to complain about regarding the cost.There is three factions in the main game, Soviets,Americans,and Germans.There isn't THAT much tank diversity and a lot of the    models are pretty ♥♥♥♥♥♥ looking. The game's graphics serve their purpose but are by no means great. The Tiger tank models,for example,are abysmal. The turret on the tigers isn't even there. This is a pretty noticable problem seeing as you will be fighting a LOT of these and in one mission you play as one.Also,the tank treads are not even animated.They're static textures. One thing this game does incredibly well,however, is the environments. You fight in a multitude of battlegrounds such as invading the dunes of Africa all the way to helping out the 101st in Bastogne.The AI is abysmal. The friendly tanks will just run into you and,on occasion,shoot you in the back. The enemy AI will sometimes just sit there as you obliterate them. Another problem is the tank handling. The tanks handle like Go-Karts. You may be trying to round a corner and then all the sudden you flip over. The voice acting is suprisingly good. There is absolutely no strategy involved in the game. The battles are just a rush for the repair station and then you deal with the enemies.You are able to use commands and order friendly tanks around. However,these are never very well explained even in the manual.
TL;DR
Lots of potential here but between terrible handling,graphics that leave much to desire,abhorrent AI,and the repair-rush battles this game was quite the let down.Dont buy unless you are extremely tolerant.

You'd think that if you liked the original, you would like the sequel, but I think it strays too far from what made Hotline Miami such a fun and addictive game in the first place.
In this game, the levels are bigger, but bigger isn't always better and the large open areas lead to a less concise, tactical feeling that the original game offered. I also don't remember quite so many guns being in the original game, as it feels like melee weapons are worthless trash that only serves to make it more difficult to pick up a new gun when you need one. In fact, many of your deaths in this game will be from trying to pick up a weapon only to find out that your character decided to pick up a useless melee weapon or empty gun instead, which feels like an incredibly cheap way to die. Since the levels are so much bigger this time around, it's all the more frustrating when you die to the last 1 or 2 enemies since that means there's just that much more to have to do all over again.
The fun of picking masks with different effects to change your strategy is pretty much completely gone. There are different masks to choose from sometimes, but only on specific characters in the multiple-character campaign, and even then the masks are more gimmicks than actual strategical advantages. For instance, the bear mask lets you start with 2 machine guns and 128 ammo. Great until you reach a point where you have 10 bullets left and you realize you're not allowed to drop the guns until all the ammo is used up and are forced to leave perfectly good guns behind because of this.
The fact that thare aren't any new features or mechanics only serves to highlight what's missing from the original, so in the end I would just suggest playing Hotline Miami 1 instead, as it's a more focused and tightly designed experience. HM2's only addition is to expand the story, which is nice and all but I loved Hotline Miami for the gameplay and the story was just an interesting bonus. Here, the gameplay suffers because the story calls for a cast of several playable characters and varying environments that simply aren't fun to play through.
Oh, also the hit detection blows. Like really really bad. I don't remember it being this bad in the first game, which is weird because I assume it's the same engine.

I hate to begin a review with "That's like that other game with the following differences" but I can't help myself. This game is "heavily inspired" by Left 4 Dead with some aspects being a straight rip off. Not that this was bad though, Left 4 Dead (2) is an excellent game and Vermintide took several elements and mixed them into a better game.
The basics are the same, you have 4 players, wandering through landscapes infested with literally hundreds if not thousands common enemies and a couple special enemies. However, your goal in most cases is not just surviving, you have mission objectives. And you have classes. And meele combat. And the whole Warhammer theme.
The classplay is amazing. 5 classes, each with a different playstyle, different weapons, meele and ranged. The ranged weapons are, well, fun, but severyl limited. You don't get a metric crapton of ammo to carry around with you in most cases. Instead, you have to think carefully when you shoot and when you slash/bludgeon. And unlike L4D, there's no infinite ammo pile at every critical chokepoint. You get an infinite ammo pile every now and then, but be glad when you get a finite ammo pile at the final battle. But hey, we have meele weapons! The meele system isn't as deep as in Killing Floor 2 (I'm spoiled), but it's enjoyable nontheless, it has just enough deph to fit the whole "On the run" aspect (you don't always have the time to prepare that perfect swing) and there's genuine enjoyment in swining a badass war hammer through a horde of ratlings, taking a couple skulls along your swing. Speaking of, the gore is a bit over-the-top and fits well with the atmosphere. Which is fantastic! I could literally not care less about Warhammer, but the character design, the enemy design, map design, sound scape, wow. Just wow. The combat suits the design as well, it's a tad slow-paced, the beforementioned war hammer surely takes it time to land a swing, guns are typically single-shooters (with severely limited ammo), there's that sense of deliberate combat. You have to consider every action instead of just winging it. Well, you can do that on the easy difficulty, but that's not much fun.
All things considered, if you're into a first-person game that combines shooting, visceral meele combat, hordes of enemies, coop and objectives, getting Vermintide is a no-brainer.
The game plays just like L4D, But it doesn't feel like it. so if you liked killn zombies! Then you'll love killing skaven and looking for the best weapons that you can use to bash skaven skulls in!

This game has a lot of good qualities, but many of them are nullified by the utter crap that is the AI and lack of diversity in gameplay.
Many of you will enjoy the feel of commanding your own tank force, as well as knowing that your air force are fighting furiously in the skies above you, and I good thing to notice is that the skybox literally looks almost like real sky.
However, know that every main gun you get behaves the exact same way, such as my 20mm Kwk having the exact same effect as a 75mm Kwk. Every shell also appears to be HE, which is something that drives me away from liking the tank combat.
From what I can tell, the part of your tank that a shell hits has an effect on how much damage you take. However, many times the AI tanks will charge you, then immidiatly turn around, exposing their engine (which is a 1-shot kill) and running away.
It's worth noting that in-game models seem to be made with care, as I was quickly able to distinguish a ZiS gun from a PaK gun. You can also see the differences between infantry models, as well as the weapons they carry. The tank models, however, look made in a 640x400 resolution. Seeing as how the game can run in 1366x768, they just plain look ugly.
The missions aren't very diverse. It's always a mix of "kill everything that moves," "go here," and "don't die." Thus the game gets boring very quickly. The few siege missions are set up very, very poorly. They allow you to camp around your repair and ammo supplies and kill the oncoming enemies as quickly or slowly as your little heart desires.
Overall, this isn't necessarily a
game, but it's most certainly not a good one either.

This is a pack of two games (Panzer Elite Action "Dunes of War" and "Fields of Glory") with lots of potential but excuted poorly in several ways. First, the Tiger tanks are rendered without their turrets in both games. I can't believe that wasn't caught in their quality checks. Second, the tank physics in several missions is like more like a beach ball than a multi-ton armored vehicle. If a tank from your squad runs into you, your tank is bounced off the ground or spun around like a beach ball. In one mission I was bounced into a mine field and blew up. In the D-Day mission, the Sherman rolls over easily at the slightest slope of beach. Third, the tank treads are not animated. Let me also summarize every mission: Shoot waves of enemy tanks. Expect anti-tank guns to ambush you around every corner. Find health. Find ammo. Repeat endlessly. If you are looking for strategy or variation this is not your game. Gameplay gets really tedious, especially in Dunes of War. It becomes a question of "Can I find health?" not "How can I out-think my enemy?" It's a shame really because the graphics are not bad. The voice actors are pretty good. The historical vignettes with old movie footage are pretty good too. Gameplay is OK. There are no on-screen instructions in Dunes of War so play Fields of Glory first so you learn the keyboard commands. I am still looking for that magic, amazing, well-conceived tank game you can play over and over. This is not it.

Game Title: RatzInstagib
Release Date: 28/07/16
Developer: Lino Slahuschek Publisher: Rising Star Games
Game Engine: Unity 
Reviewed On: MacOS Available On: MacOS, Microsoft Windows,
First Thoughts: I first ran into Ratzinstagibs when I was browsing the steam store and after watching the video on its store page I thought to myself “I have to play this game”. It instantly reminded me of older skill based shooters such as the Quake, Doom and Unreal series of games. Ratzinstagibs is a fast, skill based precision shooter that is reminiscent of games of the late 90s and Early 2000s. The Catch with this game is you are only given one gun, which is a one-hit kill Railgun. So if you are a type that likes to have a thousand guns to unlock this isn't the game for you.
Presentation: Ratzinstagibs art design seems to point towards the type of game this is: Basic. I am in no way saying that this looks bad, the art style is quaint and to the point. It is full of basic textures but that isn’t a bad thing for this type of Game. Most of the base maps are either a household theme or an office environment with assets to suit. However with the addition of Steam Workshop, custom maps are easily found and are integrated into the Map Voting System.
Performance: When it comes to performance this game is really hard to fault. I run this game so smoothly at 2560x1440 at 90 - 120 fps which is where it seems to be capped. The only real performance issues I experienced was due to the only games that are populated are on the European and American servers. You can occasionally find a game on the Japanese or Australian servers but you'll be lucky to find one. It may be just my shotty NBN Connection but for some reason the Ping times to the Japanese server was better than the Australian one. Otherwise, I have encountered zero issues while playing this game.
Plot: This game is a Multiplayer Only focused game which is alright given it’s premise. So if you bought this game for a decent single player campaign tough luck. There is a survival mode that you can play however its very basic and is really only good to try out your accuracy while you're on the move otherwise its just a waste of time. It is just a variety of enemies that spawn in one of the maps that you selected. If you actually want a challenge with this game mode then you will need to use the rocket jump and keep yourself moving otherwise you can just sit at one end of the map and hit the bots and dodge the slow moving projectiles.
Mechanics: This game is pretty simple in premise; Move fast, Jump high, Kill and be Killed quickly. The “rocket jump” button is quite handy and jumping all around the map like a madman is quite thrilling and it is really easy to pick up how the map layout works in with maximising your speed with the “rocket jump”. Aside from the one-shot one kill type game mode of “Instagib” there isn't much else to this game.  There are a few other game modes aside from Free For All or Duel but these are rarely populated and you'll struggle finding a game.
Combat: The combat in this game is oddly addictive with a high skill ceiling. It requires you to be mobile while accurate which is reminiscent of old school type shooters such as Quake and Doom. This game is great in the fact that 90% of the time if you get a hit on another player you will normally get the kill. Unfortunately I have noticed that you can get killed while the server takes its time to recognise your kill making your kill not valid. This again probably comes down to the connection to the EU and US servers.
Connection aside; this game is big on using its rocket jump feature to keep you mobile. If you try to play this game either like a Modern Shooter or not move at all, you will die really quickly.  You will die a lot in this game. If you are good enough to get a couple of shots on target with your railgun though, you'll do just fine.
Multiplayer: Most games you will enter into will be most likely be on the EU or US servers. Even though you are on a fairly level playing field with the “Instagib” railgun you might find yourself getting tagged out or being robbed of a kill because of the connection.
Final Thoughts: This game I found myself to be really enjoyable. Even though the major downfall of this game is its lack of players. Funny enough, when this game first hit it had tons of negative reviews, and you know what they were all complaining about? Controller support. Other than that, this game supports 60 FPS and is optimized very well, the graphics are also taken from the PS4 version yet again so while not absolutely stunning, the visuals are very clean and solid.
Anyway, if you're not that shallow and can look past the fact that the Keyboard and Mouse controls for this game are practically non existant, then what you'll find here is something truely beautiful.
Toukiden 2 is the kind of game where once you play it, you'll be witnessing the transformation of a game that was merely "another of it's genre" into it's own unique identity.
In the first Toukiden, you could very much say that it's basically Toei's version of a Monster Hunter game, with a little more focus on getting in on the action instead of gathering and preparing for the fight (whether that's a good thing or not is entirely up to preferance). But now, Toukiden 2 has pulled out all the stops and decided to go in it's own direction completely. It's a sequel that does the concept of sequels justice.
Toukiden 2 keeps all of the main mechanics from the first game that made it a MonHun style game, but improves on every aspect. Combat definitely feels a little more fluid and now there are two new weapons to try out as well. But that's where the similarities to the ever advancing MonHun series stops.
First thing you'll notice (at least in singleplayer) is that Toukiden 2 is a seemless fully open world game. There aren't any loading screens when you're exploring in the open world, only in cutscenes and mission modes. This alone changes the entire feeling of the game, it's massive and it's full of huge monsters to slay. The game then lets you take your entire party out into the open world, so now you've got a party based action heavy MonHun-like game that's set in an open world, you'll feel like it's got some Dragon's Dogma vibes going on, and that's incredible. Not only that, but in some areas, it'll feel like you're delving into something akin to Phantasy Star Online at times as well.
It starts meshing to the point where it's hard to simply compare it to one or two games of established genres and you'll see how it just becomes a crock pot of gaming ideas that forms into something that can only be Toukiden 2.
As for the multiplayer, it basically progresses like a classic MonHun game, where you just do missions, murder stuff, make stuff out of the stuff you murdered, then murder more stuff. It's a vicious cycle but it still works very well. There is however, no open world for multiplayer, but don't let that turn you away because there are what's known as "Patrol Missions" where they let you just roam around entire sections of the open world like the starting hill area or the entire zone including all the areas under the "Age of Peace" label and so on and so forth, which honestly, is more than enough considering that aside from the very first open world area, the places you can go to are absolutely massive.
Overall, I would say that unlike the first game which had an abysmal launch, if you're a fan of MonHun style games or even just Action RPG games then this one's a must buy. It takes all the things that worked in the first and improves upon everything while doing so many things new that while it may feel similar, it will also feel completely new and fresh at the same time.
TL;DR Summary
Okay so, you take Dynasty Warrirors' Style, Monster Hunter's Gameplay, Dragon's Dogma's Open World JRPG Feeling, and Toukiden's Setting, throw them all into a blender and MIX THE **** OUT OF THEM. Then you get this game. It's a mish mashed monster, but it has all the good crispy bits, and who doesn't like crispy bits?
TL;DR Basic Port Stats
- 60 FPS
- Very well optimized, runs buttery smooth
- Fullscreen basically functions as Borderless Windowed
- However the Keyboard and Mouse controls are complete trash, gonna need a controller for this one.
Oh and I forgot to mention, if you like Waifus and Husbandos, the affection system is still very much intact from the first game. Get your body ready to bathe with best girl or best guy... or both ( ͡° ͜ʖ ͡°)

Huge improvement over Toukiden 1 and Kiwami. It's taken forever for one of these Monster Hunter type games to embrace an open world design. Sure there's no mouse support, Do people honestly not have a PS3/PS4, 360/Xbone controller lying around that they can plug into their pc's? That and substantially up the world's graphics, with recent titles like Hyrule Warriors and Dragon Quest Heroes we know they're capable. Omega Force needs to step into the next generation already instead of tending to frequently hang two generations behind everyone else graphically. It's most likely the Vita that's holding everyone back. The game is a blast though. Hopefully as they perfect the hunting game formula they can eventually prod Capcom into playing with the big dogs again where big monsters belong----on the big screen. The 3DS 800 x 240 res 4.88' screen just doesn't cut it for slaying life sized dragons and it's a shame.

Gears of War with robots.
A 3rd person cover shooter, where you can dismember robots arms and legs as they attack you, and watch them crawl along the floor trying to get to you because you shot its legs off. Shooting the head off robots causes them to malfunction and shoot at the other robots.
The gunplay in binary domain is satisfying with the guns having some weight to them and the robots reacting appropriately to the bullets you hit them with. You have some teammates to play with and can order them to fire, charge, regroup or retreat. I didn't find that they actually killed alot of robots, but I wouldn't call them useless, they do get kills.
Its unforunate that this game has come to be known for the voice recognition aspect, because its far from necesssary to actually use this system to enjoy the game, and I found that even with the relatively good mic I have (Blue Snowball) I would get the wrong communication recognized. This is important because comms can alter your teammates perception of you, which matters because there is a sort of "karma" system where you can gain favor with your teammate or have them dislike you based on how you respond to them.
I would actually recommend playing this shooter with a controller. I found the keyboard controls clunky, especially trying to melee, cover and switch weapons. The color feels much more natural and I had no problem getting headshots and shooting accurately with an xbox controller.
Overall this was a fun game with a story that I actually enjoyed. Usually I skip cutscenes (which you CAN do in this game) but here I didn't because I thought the story was pretty cool.

I was looking for a replacement for an aging Left4Dead 2, and set my sight on this game.
From a few hours of playing the game, it looks promising with so many 'buts'. And I really wanted to give this game a thumb up, I do, but I can't because of those 'buts'.
The game is easily comparable to Left4Dead 2 but without PvP so from the get go it's already at disadvantage. And when I look at the fact that the game requires DLC purchases to open the map.....
I also would like to mention that melee-ing enemies is too superior, unlike in L4D. While a class is definitely, and must be, taken into account, melee is in-arguably powerful and it doesn't make sense since it shouldn't be - weapons should be far more superior.
And don't forget that a game of this level doesn't have Workshop Support. It is moddable to certain extent (just like 'Quality of Life modpack'), but no access to Workshop support for new level creations doesn't help. This kind of game benefits from the existence of Workshop, I assure you. Left 4 Dead is a prime example for this.
I have slight FPS problem but it's understandable as PC has wide arrays of hardware combos, but the game could also do with loading time improvements and the installation size which is, le gasp, 40 GB+.
All those negatives then bring down the impact, playerbase. It's easier to find matches on L4D2 than on this game for my region, which is ironic since the game's relatively new and L4D2 is pretty old at this point. I reckon the DLCs had big effect on this and snowballed to the reduction of playerbase. If you look at the steam stats you'd understand.
It's unfair if I keep listing the negative points, so I'll give a list of what I like from the game and would like the sequel to improve upon what's good:
- Level up system
- Crafting/Forging system
- Quick Search and Lobby options
- Achievements, Cloud Support, Trading Cards
Honestly, out of all options, the DLCs really killed my interest in the game. Had it been only cosmetic DLCs, I'd have given this a pass as it was 50% yes - 50% no in my mind.
4/10 - get it when on sale and pay attention if you can bear with the limitation when you don't purchase the content DLCs.

Layers of Fear, a horror game where the environments tell a story, and leave you with an ever building sense of dread. I liked it even if it was shorter than I would have expected. is a very scary game -- but perhaps not for the reasons that you'd expect.
Unlike other games in the genre,
does not rely heavily on sudden full-screen "jump scares".  In fact, quite the opposite; the vast majority of the events that unsettled me were only seen out of the corner of my eye, or happened while I wasn't looking at all.  Such moments are cleverly woven into the game's story, and whether you choose to turn around and investigate or push onwards may have consequences.
The game is quite short, but how short depends largely on your curiosity.  The main character's tortured past unfolds slowly, as you collect objects scattered through his house and listen to the memories that they prompt; I expect that an uninterested player could finish it in less than an hour.
I don't recommend the DLC, though.  It's very little like the main game, and completely unnecessary.

Anyhow, very enjoyable horror game. Sadly unity engine, and had constantly weird bug. (spinning camera).

Here's my 8 hours take on the game.
First, the boring stuff:
- No mouse support
- It's locked in 60 fps
- It's an overall superior port to the original Toukiden but it's still a port and not something created from the ground up
- Only consider this game if you have a controller; Keyboard controls are pure garbage
Now let's talk about the game.
They finally did it.
They took the Hunting genre created and maintened for years and year from Monster Hunter and created a "clone" that still is pretty much a clone in certain aspects while bringing a whole new flow to the gameplay.
You got your typical "grab the quest, hunt the monster" you are expecting from the genre but then you got a fully fledged action RPG on top of it and presented as the main course. This is one of the better open world experiences, I've stumbled into some secrets that opened new ways of bulding my own character in the game. It felt like the more I explore, the cooler the secrets I find. I'll relay this gameplay loop as my experience:
Behind a massive boulder from the souther region of the "Age of Honor" region of the map, there was this small shrine. I was lost, trying to find a way to reach my destination that did not travel in the "Underworld" cave system because if I did, my character would be poisoned by the Miasma and die.
So I stopped and decided to check on the shrine. There I found a figure of Japanese/German history I've never even heard about, Siebold (Philipp Franz von Siebold).
The character explains why his spirit was trapped there and asks for you to track a specific Demon with your "Oni Slaying Vision" and bring one of it's part for him to analyze.
So I track the creature, have a climatic showdown in the heart of an abandoned city and manage to bring the part to this Siebold fellow, who then is absorbed. He is one of the "Mitama", spirits that customize how you play the game. Think armor skills from Monster Hunter on steroids.
This partircular Mitama had a bunch of synergy with the Whip weapon, so I decided to try. Aiming explosive kunai tem smashing them with the whip and blowing up specific parts of the monster quickly turned me into an addict. And it's all thanks to this random thing I ran on the scenery that gave me the push to try different weapons, builds and approachs.
So far, this game is more than a step up from Toukiden 1 - It's a unique and refined take on the Hunting genre. When it tries to be copy cat Monhun it stumbles, but when it's being itself, it's an all around fun time. Let's see if the feeling persists through my next 8 hours.

I got this game during one of Sega's giveaways and at it sat in my library for the longest time. Now that I have recently beaten it for the  backlog's sake, I can confirm that this was a really really fun game.
Binary Domain is a third person shooter set in Japan in which you are a soldier on a covert op and you get to kill robots. There is more of a story, but for me, I just like the fact that I am in futuristic Tokyo and I get to shoot lots and lots of robots. You get to team up with a memorable cast of characters and while you don't get lots of backstory, you definitely will form bonds with them. There is a trust system in which how you handle yourself in combat and in various dialogs will effect how much your comrades trust you, and ultimately, which ending you'll get. Oh yes, there are two endings.
The look of this game is great. I never had any problems with lag and glitches. The voice acting was well done, but some of the dialog was repetitive, especially during combat. The music and sounds are great in keeping up with the non-stop action of the game. While you are mostly fighting, there are pop up scenarios that almost feel like mini-games throughout the campaign, such as escape scenarios and car chases. The game really has an arcade kind of feel at times, and it helps keep it fun not stressful.
The only negative are the controls. Sometimes the controls are not clear. There were many times when I was told to press "M". Well, after looking at an online guide, I found out the game meant "mouse", not the "M" on the keyboard. There are multiple forums on the internet asking for help in various situations due to poor control layout, especially in timed scenarios.
I'm really glad that I got this game. Now that I know how fun it is, I would definitely recommend it at full price. It's fun, has an entertaining story, cool characters, and a great setting. There is definite replayability since different comrades leads to different ends. I know at least another playthrough is definitely in the future.

In our second season, We did far better. You bickered less, and worked better as a team unit. We were able to climb the ranks far higher then we expected based on last seasons proformance. We fought and battled our way to a third place finish overall in our second year together. It was an amazing year with a few race wins and a few more podium finishes. But it still wasn't enough.
With one year remaining on all of your contracts, We got right back to work for our third season in Europe. We could feel it in the air, This was OUR year. With contracts winding down, and no one sure where we would be this time next year. Everyone gave it their all. Trying to push for the win this year.
It was our hardest year yet. Fighting back and forth with Dragon Racing. The entire season only a few points seperating our two teams. They had more race wins then we did. Totaling 7/5. But we had better team positioning, often coming in 2nd & 3rd. Points were close the entire season, but we finally managed to pull ahead with points in the last two races.
We WON! After three long years together, we won the European Series Championship!

But our celebrations were short lived, Everyones contract was up in a month. No one knew where they were going to be for next season, or even if they would have work. You were not happy with the contract I offered and insited I pay you more given that you just won the European Series.
I reluctently agreed, and we were set for another 2 years in the new Asia Pacific Championship.

No one expected that. Not even us. You all were so elated to know how good our team had gotten in just four years. Hong again won over Shen Qi. With a dominating 65 point gap.
Again I was approched about moving up to a higher challenge. I accepted it instantly in excitement. This is what I had been working for. This is what WE had been working for.
That brings us to now. The start of season 5. Our FIRST season in the Highest competition out there. The World Series.
I want to thank each and every one of you from the bottom of my heart. We have had great times together, and some not so great ones. But we were able to grow as individuals and as a team. Without you I don't think I could have made it here.
And now, Without any further Adue. I want to introduce you all, to your NEW REPLACEMENTS! In this season and all seasons to come after. I will need better drivers, desginers and mechanics if I want any chance to win.

Not really sure what I was expecting from this game, but had a 50% off code, so commited to the purchase.
I love the football manger franchise, and was hoping for a cut down version of that game. Unfortunately this is to cut down for my liking.
Staff Options:
As the game stands there are limited race series options and very limited actual team management availble. Pretty much just hire or fire your drivers, desinger and the mechanic for each driver. I really was hoping for more staff options and of a more detailed breakdown on the relevant traits.
In Race:
I've completed 3 seasons so far, and find the game very repetitive. What tyres do I want, X amount of laps, X amount of fuel in the car gives you an estimate of how many pits you are going to do.
Though more may be required if your parts aren't very reliable.
Car Prep:
You basically have 3 things here:
1. Designer - please create me a new part (obviously the better designer, and more money you have the better the part)
The are limited options on risk/reward with the parts. And you only have 1 resource designing 1 part for 1 car at a time.
2. Mechanics - Post race repairs, and between race tuning of parts for performance and reliability.
3, Car Design - limited options on actual build of car (how much money you want to spend with suppliers) and is done at the start of each season. Apart from that what (basic) colour scheme and livery you want and the occasional change of sponsor.
All in all, a few clicks at the start of the season, a couple in between for new parts and then telling the drives how far to push the car or pit during the race itself. I wasn't expecting (and didn't want) anything to complicated on car design (not being a mechanic myself), but a couple of clicks and sliders didn't make this the game for me....

Only played into the game 4 hours but I'm already enjoying the hell out of it. A lot has been improved, including the landscapes. No loading between any rooms anymore because everything is already loaded. I was skeptical about the whole "open-world" thing but it seems to have been implemented very well.
Not only have two new weapon types been added (Sword and shield, chain whip) but all the other weapon types have had new moves added to them further increasing their viability and adding something to draw you back into those types so you're not spending all your time with the two new ones.
The is also a very VERY clean port. I had Kiwami on the PS4 so I can't speak for the PC version but this game runs smooth as silk on my rig. Loading times are also ridiculously short as well which is a wonder as all the ages are linked together into one giant map with no seperate "room" loading like in Kiwami.
The Demon-Hand thing seems just a tad gimmicky to me, though. I'm still trying to learn all it's ins-and-outs but I hardly use the damn thing.
EDIT: I've used it a bit more. It has other functionality like being able to grapple up to higher ledges you can't jump on which is pretty nice but the other functions of the Demon Hand seem to trivialize fights against large oni. It's way too good.
The characters aren't as compelling as the original cast in Toukiden: Age of Demons but they get pretty damn close. Of course I'm also not very far in so I may grow to love them like I did the original cast. I do really like Benizuki though, she's pretty rad.
EDIT: Got a bit further into the game and the characters are starting to get fleshed out more. I'm starting to grow to like them even more now. Writing is still absolutely solid.
This part doesn't affect me as I use controller but it's a tad bit silly to not have mouse support on a PC game. I'm also wondering if this is intentional or not as I've seen some text in the game that wasn't quite... right? One of the screenshots explaining something was a Japanese screen shot and when sending my machina out on a survey the survey time was shown as "Survey Time" not "long" "very long" or anything like that. A few things just seems a tad weird to me so the lack of mouse support may not be intended.
All in all a very good game and a very good sequel to the original. I highly recommend picking it up.

This game at it's current state is pretty darn good. And I say this because of many reasons like:
1. The story is intriguing and it has that little something that keeps you going through it. They reward very good loot(some of them) when you replay them at max level, which is 60. Yes, you can replay almost every episode(missions). New episodes are added regularly. The story captures the feel of the Star Trek universe pretty well.
2. The combat is good at the start, but it can get boring if you don't have a good build. There are many builds out there and there is one for you for sure. Ground combat is not the best, but not the worst either.
IMPORTANT!  The game relies on DPS a lot. It is possible to be a healer/tank, but you won't influence the battles that much.
3. The game is massive. Sector Space is huge with a lot of Systems including Sol System, Qo'Nos, DS9, Drozana Station and the new Delta Quadrant is awesome. There are tons of things to do in the game, from crafting to grinding Energy Credits(in-game currency) to building your Fleet Space Station and other Fleet buildings.
4. One of the best things with this game is that you can get Zen(the most important currency) in two ways:
a. Buy Zen with money. OR
b. Grind Dilithium, which is made from quite a lot of activities in-game. There is a Dilithium exchange market controlled entirely by players like a stock market or a bank. You buy Zen for Dilithium or vice-versa. That makes Dilithium a very important currency. You are capped at making 8.000 dilithium per day per character though. But you can make other characters and transfer the dilithium to the character you want. Zen is the only currency account-wide.
