Binary Domain is an Action game by the creators of the Yakuza series. From what I've heard, that series is super strange but enjoyable - while Binary Domain is enjoyable at moments, don't expect the same level of strangeness here. Instead, Binary Domain is a game about Big Bad Killer Robots in a dystopia, being fought by a team of humans and some robots to stop them. As it is a mid-2010s' game, cover-based shooting is used frequently. As the player assumes the role of the lead commander of their group, Binary Domain mixes in-game actions with voice commands you can feed it to give your squad members feedback and orders, but you can also damage your relationships with your squadmates with these commands.
So, right off the bat, Binary Domain has a good plot. Kind of mysterious, intriguing, and neatly wrapped up. The best non-gameplay related part of Binary Domain is its premise, which it executes well in some areas, not so many in others. The shooting feels chunky, but not in a bad way. The robots serve as nice enemies and are challenging to take down as they're pure metal and electronics. The squad relations system works decent enough, and the outcomes are also brilliantly handled.
The game controls very well on a keyboard and never made me feel sick, and it looks decent (despite the fact that my PC is a total potato), especially for the time being. Gamepad controls aren't bad as well, and I never really noticed any disadvantages for either playstyle (k+m/gamepad).
Binary Domain is a great game that deserves more attention than it ever gets, BUT... the biggest dealbreaker, no matter who you are, is the voice commands system. To say that this feature is inconsistent would be an understatement and it's clear that this was developed at a time where voice commands weren't really there yet in terms of overall functionality. That's not to say that modern Siri or that Amazon thing or that Google thing work well, but at least it understands what you're saying for a good chunk of the time. Here, random breathing, sighing, moaning, or any other slight sound that your microphone can pick up can be interpreted in may ways - mainly including insults (for me, at least), which, as mentioned in the pros, can impact that way your game plays if overused. It doesn't matter if you bought a 900 dollar microphone to play this game - the tech is still super inconsistent. Often times, when testing out the commands in a setup menu, it wouldn't understand me even when saying the words as slow, clear, and precise as possible.
But, oh wait! The developers thought of this and put in a no-mic commands functi- oh wait, that's total dog♥♥♥♥♥too. Yes, you don't have to play Binary Domain with a mic, but you won't be getting the full experience, either. Your commands are super limited in no-mic mode, and even if they aren't, the interface for the commands menu is almost non-existent so it's nearly impossible for me to tell if there are more commands than the first ones I see. This would have been a great way to help keep the game from aging too terribly, but I feel that this is an area that's severely lacking. If SEGA and its assortment of developers ever revisit this little gem, and godspeed to them if they do, this - besides the voice commands - is an area they really need to patch up.
Aside from this, a bit of a nitpick I have is that it does get repetitive after some time. It does introduce new concepts here and there, but when that stops, the cover based shooting can get bland after the 50th time.

BattleRush is a basic WW2 shooter with a small variety of weapons vehicles and a basic but fairly intuitive. The game is still in alpha, and plays like one.
This wont be a full review, because it cant be. The game is still in alpha, so with the very frequent updates adding and fixing things, which is good, things are going to change.
The game overall at the moment should not be played competitively. The mechanics aren't smooth, the combat is sometimes unresponsive and the gamemode is flawed and overly basic - AT THE CURRENT STATE. What this game is now, is the foundations for a GREAT game, the combat although fidly at the moment, will feel very satifying when it is developed some more. The building aspect of the game, though minimal now, is still enough for it to impact the game greatly and is the base for a very easy to use building system comparable to the one in Fortnite.
The physics and destruction isn't the best, but works. With development, it will create some cool and tactical battles while playing.
The weapons are fairly balanced but can feel unresponsive and hard to hit shots with certain weapons in certain situations, for example bot action rifles, however with some tweaking to hit registry and movement this can feel a lot nicer. Grenades dont feel too useful except in buildings, which from experience combat barely happens in single buildings. This can be fixed by making them go a little further when thrown.
The crafting and gathering is a good idea, but basic. This allows it to not get in the way and I think it should stay this way. Soem things are harder to craft and gather than others, but not overly difficult to the point where you dont see action. Still, I'm sure later people will be more serious and assign squads to do this job for the team.
There is currently a single gamemode, with more to definately come because the current is probably the weakest point of the game. The overall objective of the game is to destory the enemy base, and thats it. Obviously this will be tweaked, as it is just the early playable test version, but more smaller sub-objectives need to be added sooner rather than later.
Overall, I definately recommend giving this game a try even if its just for the one time. I'd also say to come back in a few weeks to a month as I think by then the game will be much better, as its still in its very early stages. This is fine and all you can do is give it time to mature as with some more time the game will be very good. Cheers

So far I've played two games and beat the game with my friends on apprentice with the default 3 classes and killed all the scourges except for the old man. Here are my thoughts on the game so far.
Pros:
+ Incredibly fun with friends, especially if you're going in blind and discoving things for yourselves
+ Each fight and enemy feels unique in its mechanics and how they play out, especially the scourges and final fights
+ The simpler visuals work well and don't detract from the enjoyment of the game
+ Enjoyable loot based gameplay that makes you strategize around the items that randomly drop similar to other games like Diablo 2
Cons:
- Currently the in-game explanations of some item abilities and mechanics can be extremely poor, such as items simply listing "Inspire", "Encourage", "Elite Sneak", and "Elite Flee" as abilities with no explanation of what these words actually do appearing upon mousing over. While this is fine with things such as "Immune to Burning" and "Immune to Shock" some abilities and effects could definitely use some additional description.
- Extremely unstable on Macs, with frequent crashes and disconnections. Only me and my friend who played on macs experienced these problems though, so Windows users should be fine.
- A problem revealed by frequent crashes: the "Ironman" nature of the game is slightly ruined by the fact that the game autosaves only on the end of the host's turn. This means that if a player crashes or deliberately disconnects they can rollback poor rng and decisions up to three turn prior. This also can cause significat frustration in long dungeons, which must be done from the beginning in the case of an unexpected disconnection.
- A graphical bug that I specifically experienced was that certain elements of the world would start epileptically flashing without warning, so if you have a history of epilepsy I would strongly suggest against playing this game
Overall, if you're put off by the bugs listed here I would suggest waiting until the game is in a more stable state before playing. But even despite these pretty severe bugs me and my friends enjoyed the game even when the world started epileptically flashing and I would not refund this game just because of its instability and bugs in its early access state.

This game has many rather frustrating mechanics.  These include:
- Chances that a skill fires off are rather low (~40-60% at base stats).
- Skill chance success is disparate between enemies and players.
- Only one character can heal other characters (herbalist), which is effectively required.
- Most tactical skills are non-functional late game, rendering most tactics useless.
For me, the worst offender is the significant chance to miss on party buff skills.  I understand offensive abilities should have a chance to fail; however, party buffs having a chance to miss is a significant drawback.  Since these buffs are not OP, having a chance for failure does not seem balanced.
For many, these aspects may add to the game's lifetime, as they effectively drive a game-over and requiring a replay.  For me, these types of mechanics are merely frustrating and do not make me wish to play this game over the plethora of other games out there.
Not worth a purchase, even on sale.

I was pleasantly surprised by this game. The platforming is good and the levels are well designed and varied. The boss fights are fun, and probably the best part of the game. It is fun getting new powers, although the game hides most of them for some reason, and since they do a terrible job trying to help you with secrets, you won't find a power or two, and you will miss many upgrades, a mistake to hide away in almost impossible to find spots. The story isn't bad, and it's nice seeing all of the old classic monsters from literature. It is fun playing in two different forms, both of which act differently. Then there are the problems. People are right that aiming with selena is finnicky and annoying, especially since so many parts emphasize it. The two biggest problems are collision detection and damage reaction. The collision is terrible. I got hit many times by projectiles that were over me or past me. This is annoying when you have to fight as the wolf and you are standing next to a boss to hit him, as is your only way of damage, and you get hit for standing too close. Most games would just limit you from going forward, but here it lets you and you get hurt because its hard to find the spot close enough to damage but not get hit. The other problem as people mention is when you get hit you go flying back. This overreaction is annoying, unnecessary, and why you die basically every time. The game says you become invulnerable after being hit for a bit, but that's not actually true. You can get repeatedly hit and juggled, even in the air. If you get hit back and immediately jump forward you aren't invulnerable, you immediately get hit again. Getting juggled and auto killed when you can't do anything is annoying. It also makes it dumb because there will be a single platform you need to jump to a guy on there, so you can attack them by jumping toward them. The game seems to use this annoying area to place guys in spots where u repeatedly can't get past and keep getting kocked back or off. Also guys will throw things where you are going to jump to, which makes no sense. One other problem is sometimes checkpoints are scattered too far, and you have to do a bunch of hard precise parts in a row and you think "really guys.....". The game length is also quite good and I had fun almost the entire time. Both collision and the stupid damage response hamper this game and make it more frustrating than it should be and make parts annoying and inclined to continually repeat. People spoke of difficulty but I thought it was tough but no stupid or unfair, like a Super Meat Boy. Pick this game up, excited if there's a sequel. 7.5/10.

I come, by these means, to advise you on
. I have been playing this game since I first discovered it, in the midst of February of 2017, and I hold no intentions of quiting it anytime soon.
In a world where weapon wielding, sometimes pegleged metal men take to the skies in custom steam powered airships, you, the player, play the role of one such
.
You build your very own airship in your hangar and take flight, alone or with a crew of your own choosing, to combat other
, be it either other players or fully AI controlled airships.
In battle, one can steer the airship and man the turrets for airship to airship combat of epic proportions! Or one can simply take a more
approach, arming themselves with a variety of weapons, from carbines, to knives, to explosives and attempt to board the enemy airship in attempt to disable it from within.
Airmen is a humble game, created by a single humble person, fueled by dreams and friends. It is the culmination of 1 year and 6 months of very hard and tedious work and in more ways than one, it truly shows.
+ Consistent, simple and very appealing visual style.
+ Great variety of Small to Large parts for you to build your very own
, be it a fast, small and manoeuvrable airship, to an enourmous flying fortress with enough firepower to level a city.
+ Said parts are all 100% free and available to all players
+ Said firepower includes but it is not limited to: Gatling guns, Canons, Harpoons, metal Rams and a variety of handheld weaponry.
+ An ever expanding range of free cosmetics to customize your own metal man, from a Lord in a top hat and monocle to a barbarian clad in wolf pelts. (You can even have a pegleg!)
+ A very approachable and open minded developer that plays the game regularly and whom always welcomes any sugestions and feedback about the game in his
.
+ Weekly updates and balances.
+ A friendly and very welcoming community.
+ 4 Official game modes: Team Deathmatch, Escort, Siege and Sandbox; With easily playable custom game modes.
+ An expanding list of beautiful maps, that provide dynamic gameplay, to choose from.
+ Any player can host a server and play with his friends any time he wishes to.
+ Very user friendly HUD, controls and features, from buttons to rotate your entire airship in your hangar to detailed charts describing everything from how much mass and lift your airship has to how much steam pressure your different airship components are using.
+ Don't want just one airship? You're in luck, you can have and create as many
files as your heart desires and you never need to fear them being deleted, for they are saved in a diferent folder from the main game.
+ You and your friend made a cool airship that you want to share with each other? You can! All
files are shareable between computers and, if I'm not mistaken, operating systems.
+ This game will never feature an annoying RNG crate drop system and if it ever does, I will personally murder the developer.
+ Your imagination and creativity is the limit to what you can create!
+/- Not really a Con for myself, but some people may not enjoy this. The character animations in this game are very, very simple. I, personally, enjoy them very much as I love to see robots running and jumping around in goofy animations and the humour it provides.
- Your imagination and creativity is the limit to what you can create. But fear not, you can always ask other players for help or for an airship.
- No soundtrack, for now.
- Mediocre sound work overall, it's good, but it's not great and sometimes multiple miniguns at once can get a tad obnoxious.
- Some bugs pop up here and there. Without a proper team for the job, the dev requires playtesting and player feedback to find and correct these bugs.
- No fast part deleting system in the hangar. If you're building away and suddently need to delete a lot of parts on big constructions, you are going to have to delete them one by one.
The game can become overwhelming at first, but take it one step at a time and you will enjoy it greatly. A basic airship consists of a few balloons, some engines to power some propellers and a steering wheel, maybe a ballast or two to control vertical lift and that is literally it, anything apart from that is 100% up to you and the possibilities are nearly endless.
Airmen is a very fun and satisfying game if you happen to enjoy old airships, anything steampunk and building games. If you are familiar with the genre, imagine if you're playing Robocraft, but it's steampunk and is in the air... Oh and it's actually a good game.
Very fun to play with friends and if you ever do, I promise you that you will not regret the time spent in the game, both building and playing matches where hilarity is almost garanteed to happen.

Pretty good game, given it's stage of development.  The build mode can take some time to get used to, but it's very stable and has a lot of features that make it enjoyable (a rotate button to turn your ship around if you build it the wrong way, undo button, redo button etc.), so you rarely feel like you're fighting the build system.  Not much to report as far as the singleplayer sandbox is concerned, exept that it loads fairly quickly and makes testing ships fairly easy.
As for the main muiltiplayer mode, it still doesen't have the same stabillity that the others do, and is prone to glitches and crashing.  The gameplay itself really depends on how many players there ae and what ships they bring, but it mostly focuses on ship-to-ship combat (ships damaging eachother with ship-mounted weapons) and boarding (crew jumping onto an enemy ship, killing crew, damaging components and possibly capturing the ship).  Bugs aside, both combat systems are well-balanced and are quite fun if you have plenty of players.  However, 1v1 matches tend to take awhile and often end up being monotonous:  the game mechanics were designed for teams, not individuals.
In the end, it's a good game with lot lot of potential and is great for people who like building (I think I have spent ~100 hours building in the game before the steam release), strategy, and shooting (boarding an enemy ship feels almost like an FPS), but the game still has many glitches in multiplayer that can be limiting.

This is a great manager game. It's fun to play and very addictive. There are already enough reviews that describe the game so I will concentrate only on the negative aspects of the game.
1. Fast Forward
As in most sport manager games you can fast-forward when it comes to the match or in this case the race. There are three paces and the fastest one is still too slow. It should have a faster fast-forward.
2. Create your own drivers, mechanics, designers and race teams
You can only create a manager character. You should at least be able to create your own race teams. The game offers 3 leagues each consisting of 10 race teams. There is no option to create your own. The same applies to drivers, mechanics and designers.
3. Influence of manager character
Your own manager character has three attributes with an option for a special trait. If you don't plan on changing the race teams your attributes are pretty useless. There should be attributes like "negotiation" which affect the outcome of negotiating contracts.
4. Vote of the manager committee
Each league has a committee consisting of the managers of the race teams and each committee votes for rule changes in thier respective leagues, like which tires are allowed and stuff like that. But subjects of a rule change are predefined. You cannot initiate a rule change on your own. For example, if the rules of your league forbid refueling you cannot initiate a vote for removing this prohibition.
5. Turn down Sponsor Contracts
You cannot turn down sponsor offers. You have to wait until the offer expires.
6. THE BIGGEST NEGATIVE ASPECT
There is no driver with a similar name (due to license issues) and corresponding talent to Michael Schumacher! I mean, honestly? A motorsport game whithout the legend of legends? It's like playing a physics game without Einstein or Newton.
In the main menue of the game there is a section called "Workshop" that is labeled "Under construction" and "Coming soon". So I hope some of the above mentioned aspects will be rectified.

I've been waiting a long time for a new f1 manager game to come out and was pleasantly surprised to come across this title. I've played both Grand Prix Manager and Grand Prix World and this game surpasses both in playability, features, sound and graphics and it can only get better. Since Xmas I've played 181 hours, its highly enteraining and enjoyable. The fact that it lacks FIA licence does not detract from this at all, I thought it would spoil the fun but it's prohibative at all.  There's lots to do between races, hiring staff, upgrading parts and buildings , improving marketability to attract better sponsers, Hiring designers and mechanics who specialise in certain components. Throughout the season, every 56 days,  the GMA, that you are a member of, votes on proposed rule changes that take effect the following season i.e. faster pit stops, no refuelling, more races, different tracks, what components are spec and which are developed through the season. The interviews are a bit meh and repetitive  as well as the comments from fans and the press, they need more variety. The tracks are well designed and some are identical to real life like the Milan race is really Monza. The graphics are great but there's only 1 camera view, you can rotate it and zoom in/out but thats it. You can't get in too close to the action or see your car or driver in any detail. Hopefully more camera views will be added later. An impressive start, I have high hopes for this game and look forward to further updates and improvements.

The game decides if your drivers crash or not, no matter what you do. Reason behind this: the game tries too hard to be exciting, by incorporating random events, and not to be just a tech-fest for the F1-tech-nerds. These "random" events -which most likely target the human player- are in consequence so drastic that your season can and will be f*ed up in matter of 3 laps. I've never seen an AI driver collide three times and the victim of the collision taking 3 penalties. But my drivers magically have to. The effect of this nonsene? --> No income from sponsors, losing points on the leaderboards an in the end losing out on price money at the end of the season. In a game where money is all, this is a harsh way of creating tension, atmosphere and entertainment. In effectu you linger very long in the bottom series and the whole racing business becomes a drag and grind. I have the feeling the game tries hard to keep your progress in balance, and not let you make an "jumps", by which it negates any wise decisions you made. Minesweeper feels fairer that this.
Also several UI decisions are inept/unsophisticated: after every loading screen the short "video" with the series enblem. After 3 season this gets really annoying. The intro videos are not skippable. The training session starts whith the time ticking, not paused, which would be the default since the training is limited by time and unduly precious.
Further weird stuff you regularly encounter in the game: the nonsensical interviews. There are seemingly only 2 types of interview you can give with no real effect. So, just skip 'em. Seen one, seen all. The illegal parts stuff is also fairly unbalanced. Get caught too often and punished too lenient. How about get caught more seldom but when, then you should feel it.
I could go on 'bout this game and its features for much longer.
In the end it is sad that the game is so flawed and unbalanced, since there is no good manager game out there at this time.
Maybe the devs update this product and balance it out a little bit but in this state it gets boring too fast.

Great addictive fun game, even with its frustrating drawbacks
Pros:
Off Race features:
upgrade your cars with up to 6 different catagories of parts
upgrade your buildings, build new ones, and enjoy the heaps of rewards they bring
research new tech, unlock new and improved parts for your cars
hire and fire staff as you see fit, scout new talent, make a winning team
In Race features:
Implement team orders, increase power output at the cost of fuel, increase overtaking/aggression at the cost of tyre wear
strategise pit stops, will you change to a new set of tyres, refuel the car, repair a part, or try for 1 more lap
work out a winning formula, every race demands a very precise combination to win.
cons:
These you will find are the only real issues, and perhaps will be ironed out in the future:

This game is going to either be a hit or miss for you. And I'm gonna explain why.
This game is hard, not skill wise but mainly because of everything being heavily rng based. Everything requires a roll. Need that one last hit on the boss before he aoe kills you all? Whoops, sorry you failed an 80%+ chance roll to hit him. This could cause mass frustration, because rather than losing based on bad skills, you lost because of bad luck. This will happen multiple times during the game.
Events that happened are also random, sometimes your playthrough could be super lucky and relaxing with minimal scourge event happening. Sometimes a scourge event could happen before you can even go to the glittering mines quest. There are other mini encounters that can ambushes you, rob you of your items or golds, or just completely destroy you.
This game definitely has a unique style. They are trying to simulate dice rolls but based it on % roll system. But it's definitely not for everyone. There's a lot of people out there who dislike things being heavily rng based. It's almost like every action is a gamble in this game. Even if you have a strategic plan set in mind, a single miss roll will throw that off.
But if you are a fan of rpg+pseudo dnd style games, then this is for you. Although it won't be as forgiving as dnd. If you have a friend to play with (unlike me :() you'll probably have a fun time as well.
Side note:
This game is in early access for a reason. Many things are heavily unbalanced, especially with classes and party system. Every playthrough requires a herbalist. No herbalist = you won't make it far. Is it beatable without herbalist? Probably but I haven't encountered any myself. So if you are hoping for a fun time mixing and mashing classes together to go on an adventure, then think again. Because you are forced to play in a certain style in order to win. (This is the biggest con for me, as I enjoy variety in parties - which is what I loved about DnD, zero limitations).

This game was a little bit of a heartbreaker for me - simply because it is so obvious that this team has talent. The visuals, artistic style, and production values all seem top-notch. However, everything else about the game is kind of mediocre.
You play as a father who experiences visual and auditory hallucinations. He seems to conflate visual art with his actual life. You explore the home, learning about your wife, your daughter, and your art career. Every once in a while, you find an item of some sort that will apparently help you complete a painting that you are working on. Once you find the item, the painting you are working on gains a few new details, and the item is then displayed in a cabinet. Afterwards, you set off again. After finding the second item, it becomes obvious that you will end up finding as many items as there are openings in the cabinet. The game is basically linear, with all routes blocked but the way forward. Find an item and add a detail, rinse and repeat.
The game has a lot of jump scares, but these were typically rather well done, as jump scares go. My favorite part of the game consisted of a "haunted" doll you were chasing running into a wall. If you're reading this, you should look it up on youtube - it's a hoot.
The game could have benefitted from a better writer. Why should I care about this man? More efforts should be taken to humanize him. What were he and his wife like when they initially married? The game could have also taken some cues from Gone Home. You can still have me exploring this home, but perhaps let me find my own way forward and explore it at my own pace.
I know that this team has a better game in them, and I plan to try their latest release (at the time of this writing), Observer.

Binary Domain is an Action game by the creators of the Yakuza series. From what I've heard, that series is super strange but enjoyable - while Binary Domain is enjoyable at moments, don't expect the same level of strangeness here. Instead, Binary Domain is a game about Big Bad Killer Robots in a dystopia, being fought by a team of humans and some robots to stop them. As it is a mid-2010s' game, cover-based shooting is used frequently. As the player assumes the role of the lead commander of their group, Binary Domain mixes in-game actions with voice commands you can feed it to give your squad members feedback and orders, but you can also damage your relationships with your squadmates with these commands.
So, right off the bat, Binary Domain has a good plot. Kind of mysterious, intriguing, and neatly wrapped up. The best non-gameplay related part of Binary Domain is its premise, which it executes well in some areas, not so many in others. The shooting feels chunky, but not in a bad way. The robots serve as nice enemies and are challenging to take down as they're pure metal and electronics. The squad relations system works decent enough, and the outcomes are also brilliantly handled.
The game controls very well on a keyboard and never made me feel sick, and it looks decent (despite the fact that my PC is a total potato), especially for the time being. Gamepad controls aren't bad as well, and I never really noticed any disadvantages for either playstyle (k+m/gamepad).
Binary Domain is a great game that deserves more attention than it ever gets, BUT... the biggest dealbreaker, no matter who you are, is the voice commands system. To say that this feature is inconsistent would be an understatement and it's clear that this was developed at a time where voice commands weren't really there yet in terms of overall functionality. That's not to say that modern Siri or that Amazon thing or that Google thing work well, but at least it understands what you're saying for a good chunk of the time. Here, random breathing, sighing, moaning, or any other slight sound that your microphone can pick up can be interpreted in may ways - mainly including insults (for me, at least), which, as mentioned in the pros, can impact that way your game plays if overused. It doesn't matter if you bought a 900 dollar microphone to play this game - the tech is still super inconsistent. Often times, when testing out the commands in a setup menu, it wouldn't understand me even when saying the words as slow, clear, and precise as possible.
But, oh wait! The developers thought of this and put in a no-mic commands functi- oh wait, that's total dog♥♥♥♥♥too. Yes, you don't have to play Binary Domain with a mic, but you won't be getting the full experience, either. Your commands are super limited in no-mic mode, and even if they aren't, the interface for the commands menu is almost non-existent so it's nearly impossible for me to tell if there are more commands than the first ones I see. This would have been a great way to help keep the game from aging too terribly, but I feel that this is an area that's severely lacking. If SEGA and its assortment of developers ever revisit this little gem, and godspeed to them if they do, this - besides the voice commands - is an area they really need to patch up.
Aside from this, a bit of a nitpick I have is that it does get repetitive after some time. It does introduce new concepts here and there, but when that stops, the cover based shooting can get bland after the 50th time.
Shooting, combat, story, length are this game's pros. So 5/5 would buy again.

I had played the demo of this a while ago, and felt then that it had decent, if generic, third person cover-based shooter gameplay and a weird voice-activated squad command system that I didn't expect to use.
Turns out that that was a completely correct assessment that nevertheless managed to completely miss the point.
Binary Domain tells the story of a covert task force sent into Japan to investigate the source of Hollow Children, robots indistinguishable from humans that actually believe that they are human until they are activated. The perfect sleeper agents, who have been popping up across the world recently.
All clues point to a mysterious robotics company, led by a director that hasn't been seen in public in decades.
If that feels generic then you would be correct, the game hits a bunch of tropes over the course of its ~15 hour campaign.
In much the same vein your team doesn't consist of international characters, but rather of international stereotypes.
The arrogant American, the bro-tastic African American, the sarcastic Brit, the smooth French one, the stoic Chinese one.
Players are unfortunately locked in as the arrogant American, but are free to choose which characters they bring on missions (up to two, only ones they've already encountered) which covers roles of the team that you don't want to take care of yourself.
Don't feel like sniping? Bring the sniper. Prefer sniping instead? Leave her home and bring an assault character instead that will draw fire as you pick off enemy robots from a distance.
Yep, robots. All opposition you'll face, except for some very few exceptions, will be robotic creations of the robotics conglomerate. This might sound boring, but it allows for some very nice destruction systems where you can disable parts of your opponents, changing their behaviours. The generic humanoid variants will crawl around if you shoot off their legs and will start shooting their allies instead of you if you manage to shoot their heads off.
Your squad mates will comment on everything you do, from yelling out requests for assistance to compliments on successful takedowns to talking about recent plot developments. You are able to respond to these, theoretically by using voice commands but for the people that couldn't be bothered (like me) there are also keyboard / controller responses available. They way you interact with your squad mates will raise or lower their opinion of you which does... something.
I've only completed one playthrough, so I'm not quite sure what things could all have gone differently, but I feel that some squad members coming to my rescue and a romance subplot were optional things that I managed to trigger by which squad members I favoured.
This means that my opinion of the ending that I got might be completely irrelevant to your potential playthrough, but I
liked the ending.
In fact, my opinion of the game almost consistently got higher and higher from its slightly shaky start.
Everything slowly ramps up until an admittedly very... classic, quite predictable final boss fight that I felt was very satisfying (and, as it should be, it is definitely the hardest fight in the game, at least it was for me).
If you feel like playing a fun, highly playable action game with some clever twists and turns that gets better if you stick with it, definitely give Binary Domain a try.

You can tell that this game was made by people who enjoy motorsport for people who enjoy motorsport.  I think I have put in nearly 50 hours in barely over a week.  There hasnt been a game that monopolized my free time like that in many years.
Basically you become the team boss of an F1, F2, or F3 analog team.  You run HQ, the drivers, the car development, staff, and of course the race itself.  I wont go into great details, but its engrosssing and addictive.  Even media, rule voting, and scouting of drivers play a crucial role, and change from year to year while maintaing continuity across all divisions, teams, and, individuals.  You could concievably play forever as I am not aware of a year cap.
I prefer to start at the bottom and work my way up in games such as these, and I am currently 5 season deep with ZRT.  They are an F3 outfit that are ranked 9 out of 10 at the begining, were now up to around 4th-5th, but I am looking to move to another team soon I think as I dont see ZRT being able to win a champianship anytime soon.  Maybe a move to F2 is in my future?  Did I mention you can apply for the boss job at other teams?
All in all, its an amazing game.  The only negative thing I will say is that there are bugs.  They are not game breaking, at least not for me.  But from going through the discussion and bug reporting boards they are for some people.  However, as the majority of the reviews state, the enjoyment factor is through the roof regardless.
9/10 with the bugs, and absolute 10/10 once they are taken care of.

well this review needs to be split into two parts, one for motorsport fans, the other for everyone else.
For motorsport fans:
Looks: I does the job of pleasing your eyes with nice and detailed graphics and well selected colours, the 3D view is customizable but its got it's limits, you can turn camera around zoom in a bit and zoom out a bit. But what else would you need? well the cars are driving mostly off the natural raceline and that doesn't look good. Behavior of those machines is as strange as possible, sometimes your driver can be outbraked by a car that was miles behind... (more about it later). the looks are alltogether good but I'm worried that they focused the game on console market and you can see it pretty much everywhere.
Gameplay: If you are a motorsport fan then dont go anywhere near this game, it's the most anoying thing I've ever tried! The mechanics advice on setup is useless, there's just one practice session to get the setup sorted comepletly from scratch, the drivers are useless whatever level they are. Quali is extra short (If you're lucky you can do 3 timed laps) and you still miss any good setup, then on outlap you have to manage drivers car so by the end of lap his tires and brakes have perfect temp (with two drivers its close to impossible). Ah yeah the setup... well try to skip Practice session and check what they've done to the cars before quali, what a waste... overall the setup screen again looks too simple too much consoley, got simple settings of wing angle, tire pressure, gearbox ratio in "xx%" (why??!!), camber and suspension stiffness again in "xx%". the drivers dont give any good advice on what they need messages like "I need more wing" tell us nothing. The difference between car setups for both drivers sometimes is so different that you start to think "how the hell can they do same lap times, front wing max, rear wing minimum?!" and another one "how the hell this car can drive on that track??!!". Further on the game is missing choice of racing series, theres just one and some tracks for it nothing else, again too consoley. The race itself is as boring as you could expect from game like that, if you really lucky, you might see some sort of weird looking "fast paced" and "exiting" "action" yeah it won't cause you heart attack. Then its rain prediction, in place of giving any sort of signal that there might be rain soon you need to check the top weather bar to find out, if you dont then well take your driver into pits for new tires, as soon as he stops it will start to rain (and theres no way to swap tires on the fly in pits, only let him go and bring in again). Another thing, the lap times... you got your driver with fresh wet tires, the track is soaking, some other driver got his tires down to 30% and does laps 20 seconds faster then you!! ah and being tactical and trying to cut on pit stops or pushing makes no sense, if parts wont brake down then something else will stop you from advancing... one thing did stand out of this misery, it was the parts development, again not a lot but it actually worked.
This game hasn't got much of a proper motorsport manager...
For Non motorsport fans:
game looks good, got all the fancy graphics you might like and is simple to play, no complicated statistics or telemetry (if you know what it is). It's a simple layback game with a bit of exitement when it all comes to a roll of a dice in quali and race...
I'm really dissapointed with this game, had great expectations, was thinking of my strategy for every race, and then after first gameplay it all went down from a very steep slope... Was hoping that SEGA trademark will help it to be at least a good product, but turns out games for fans dont exist anymore, now we have to cope with universal UI for console and PC, forget all what goes into managing a racing team, forget our dreams about it. Five clicks, quick look on useless sliders and off you go.
So if youre thinking about buying it, think what you expect from it, and based on that make your decission.
Hope you wont be as dissapointed as I am.

I won't rail against this game, seeing as the reasons I didn't enjoy playing it had nothing to do with any [major] problems in execution. But I will say this, IF you intend to go about buying this game because the idea of having a had in developing a race of creature and seeing it as it evolves through the game, don't buy it.
When creating a race you are given a choice of boy parts that you can add to your micro organism to "suit" tastes, though this choice is pretty arbitrary throughout the game. I was hoping that after making some initial decisions my organism would develop based on the way I played, but instead with each new "evolution" you are given the chance to add new limbs or take away old ones, reshape your creature, change modes of locomotion, etc. This essentially takes away from the idea of a "developing" race entirely. For example, you could start (as a macro-organism) with a 1 foot purple flying furball of a creature, and at the next stage in the process completely change your creature into something resembeling a 10 giraffe like beast.
On a less personal note: The game changes play style quite a bit, which is one of the selling points for most, though I personally didn't enjoy moving on to a new play style every 45 minutes or so. It often felt like everything was rushed and lacking any real depth.  On the other hand, their are some pretty redeeming elements later on in the game if you're a RTS fan, but even this portion of the Spore felt overly simplistic.
Verdict: If you're looking for a game worth spending $20 dollars on, this is not it. Maxis makes better games that many are more likely to enjoy.
- Civ 5, The Sims, or Sins of a Solar Empire would probably offer you a greater return on your money.

First, this game is actually really fun the sounds are really good for the most part takes a bit to get used to how close things sound. there are however mild adjustments that need to be made.
The firefights in this game are really intense sometimes, i was hold up in the upstairs of a house in the middle of a field with a semi auto sniper rifle (g43 with a scope) just pelting shots at 8or so  men running across a field. we had eachother pinned for about 15 minutes, them laying machine gun fire into my building and windows, the building got railed by a rocket launcher and blew the room next to me off the house, i threw the door connecting the rooms open and used it as another sniper angle, they built a bunker system up in the field with tents in it so they could respawn and rush me multiple times.  it was great lol
Like it says "Alpha" so yes sometimes its a little laggy (shots still hit where you aim), but not very often at all is it buggy. every once in a while something like your courser getting stuck after typing in the chat (fixed by pressing tab or holding right click and moving the mouse).
Leveling is pretty easy if you just craft a lot, unlock a few classes rather quickly, smgs are deffinitly better close range but can even hit shots like 100 meters out or so, rifles can hit out to about 400 but you dont usually see people that far unless you're using a sniper rifle. anything that spawns with an explosive is pretty strong.
The tanks are a little too easy to make for how strong they are, i think they need to limit the amount of ammo you can craft and have in one tank, never having to stop and reload just pumping out 70-100 shells of cannon fire into the enemy base for like 10 minutes of work. these tanks can easily be killed by other tanks/rocket launchers, you dont find too many rockets but you can usually find a few. There is no anti tank class in the game, nothing that spawns with a rocket or the anti tank grenades. regular grenades seem to do nothing to them. (usually 2-3 people on each team rush tanks and try to charge the enemy base kinda early).
You can make bases, cement walls are kinda cheap to make which makes it fun for how big of a base you can make, there are some prefab bunkers you can place around (can also build mountable machine guns that fit perfectly to the height of the window). Sadly these dont matter too much because tanks can jus drive through your walls like nothing, and the earlier stated 70-100 shells thing.
First I have to state any gun can be looted from a random air drop (every 5 minutes or so an airdrop is flown over in a random unmarked area. you have to plane chase sometimes to find it) some of the weapons are sniper rifles, special tank killing grenades, big stacks of ammo, (2-3) five stacks of tnt, and some of the paid weapons.
Now lastly there are a few things you can pay real money for, kinda a downer because they're guns and vehicle, the strongest tank for starters (there are 3 tanks for each faction, one is an anti tank) and again 70-100 cannon shells (its a pattern tanks suck to play against right?) so if the best one is stuck behind a payment then the guy who pays kicks the crap out of your team. this is the only thing that you can pay for that can't spawn in the airdrop because you already have the plan for it, you just can't craft it unless you unlock it through the steam dlc.
Overall i would say 7.5/10, its pretty damn fun to be honest. havent even looked who the dev team is lol they might even end up deserving the dlc purchases for some things. not sure if they're doing it to help fund them or greed like the rest.
Adjustments and suggestions:
-Make tanks harder to craft
-Give tanks a little (1/4) more hp
-Make stone walls need to be shot down by a tank not just driven through. (spent 25 minutes solo building the teams base just to have 2 tanks roll in and just♥♥♥♥♥♥all over it, tripple walled with 8 stone bunkers each with 2 mounted mgs and boxes with extra rounds and grenades. 2500 stone worth of materials, you get about 1-6 per pick axe swing)
-Leave most guns how they are, decrease the accuracy on snipers by a small percent because they one shot kill fairly often and if you aim down about 1/2 centimeter youll hit every time.
-Last thing, itd be fun if you could put a lot of materials into a forward outpost, maybe a placeable building with an amount of hp half that of the normal base; the enemy would need to kill it aswell to win, instead of just shelling the crap out of your teams main base till they win (with tanks....)

Battle Rush is a free to play game, with a fairly unhealthy pay model. However, I'm not one who will judge a game for being "Pay 2 Win" right off the bat. This game is certainly not Pay 2 Win, as the guns which you recieve for paying for the classes are often sub-par to the ones that are already free. In my eyes, the only real DLC worth buying is the Anti-Tank DLC, as the Anti-Tank weaponry seems to almost never spawn when you really need it to, and a destructible environment mixed with tanks means that even if they do spawn, you'll be hard pressed to get one before being gunned down.
_____________________________
Community
The community of the game seems to be fairly standard in all honesty. Theres a solid mix of elitist "Git gud pleb", and casual players. This can make for a very frustrating game however. The game requires teamwork to be victorious, and unfortunately these groups don't mix well at all when it comes to such a vital mechanic like that. Often times the game seems to be full of people putting up walls for no real reason, other than to block or otherwise obstruct movement around the base.
_____________________________
Gameplay
Wow. Just, wow. How is it that in an FPS game, the most sub-par, awful thing, is the gun play? The Americans have an extremely unfair advantage when it comes to small arms, as the M1 Garand is superior in just about every way to the German K98. Even when it comes to the DLCs however, the American variants for their classes just seem to be overall better than those of their Axis counterparts. As it stands in it's current state (12/8/17) all an American team really has to do, is bum rush the Axis base and commence spawn killing until they can gather up enough resources for explosives (Or wait for someone with the paid DLC to just bring over the explosives they start with over). On top of the extremely unbalanced gameplay, theres an even worse glaring issue. Every single gun has the muzzle rise of a god damn mountain every time you shoot. It makes engagements less about skill, and more about guessing whether or not your enemy moved an inch or two to the left or right, or if they decided to stay still and try to control their own weapon. The only real way I can describe the awful muzzle rise, is essentially what would happen if a midget tried to free hand an automatic rocket launcher.
_____________________________
Optimization
There seems to be a running trend with games on the Unreal Engine not being able to handle their own optimization. Somehow, they've made a game that looks like a Playstation Two launch title, and made it run just about as good as one. This game has an extremely unhealthy, unstable frame rate, which can sky rocket into the 60s, or plummet into the 20s on even the best of machines. On top of that, there is a MASSIVE issue with rubber banding when it comes to servers. To their credit, the developers have mentioned this, and are planning to fix it, but at the moment it seems as though they are way too preoccupied with releasing new DLC to even bother touching it. If you've ever wanted to find out why people were complaining that even Battlefront 2 couldn't handle its dwindling community, this is a pretty good look at what they are going through over there.
_____________________________
Final Thoughts
The game has potential, but some massive issues need to be fixed. The art style makes it look like just about everything is blending together, and the constant meshing of dull blues and greens makes the entire game look like one big blob. On top of that, the issues with lag, and the DLC system (Which is bordering on Pay2Win) are going to really need to be fixed.
Devs, you have a gem in your hands. Don't ♥♥♥♥ it up with a focus on monetizing the game like your current trend is making me believe. Prove me wrong, and turn this game into a ten.

tl;dr
An excellent rogue-like rpg.  Unfair and infuriating.
This game.  Where to start?
Pros:
* highly addictive gameplay with outstanding rpg mechanics.
* good loot system with paper doll equipped items and well designed item attributes.
* cool-looking procedurally generated hex grid map.
* the few wins you achieve will be extremely satisfying!
Cons:
* You are VERY unlikely to beat this game (even on easiest difficulty) without a good number of unlocks.  Be prepared to grind a few losses to build up your lore (currency for unlocking characters, items, and events).
* I'm 100 hours in and have yet to beat the game on Journeyman difficulty which is one step up from easiest difficulty.  The game is designed to beat you, troll you, and enrage you (HULK SMASH !!!).
* combat UI is a bit wonky, but is servicable once you get used to it.
More gory details:
Saw this streamed on Twitch and decided it was worth (part of Steam Holiday sale).  After first few playthroughs on easiest difficutly I was questioning my purchase.  I pride myself a gamer... why am I getting my bootie handed to me so hard?  Is the game rigged?  What's up with my Hunter only proc'ing his passive (automatic crit) when the enemy has 1 hp?  Cool - the game has gelatinous cubes !  wait... did it just dissolve my armor ???!!!  Why are my weapons so sucky?  Why is everything so expensive at the markets and vendors?
I had many questions, and few solutions.  But, after a few more games and my first victory, I was hooked for good.  Presently, after calming myself from my latest rage quit, I grind away at Journeyman difficulty trying different party compositions and laughing/crying/raging when the game trolls me.
If you enjoy rogue-like games, rpgs, challenging strategy scenarios, and can sometimes appreciate it when you are being trolled by the developers then do NOT hesitate - buy this game immediately.

The game starts by asking you to press the "?" key... Yeah, but this doesn't mean the question mark key, apparently it means "any key" - but the question mark is not an any key! So it's "almost any key" then... Let's try space... OK, that works.
So the game starts, and you're shown your controls. Hm, the pictures of the 1, 2, 3, 4 keys are laid out in a square, like the controller's d-pad. Besides, the game is unplayable with a gaming mouse, and there are no sensitivity settings or anything (there are no settings in general, so this is just one drop in a huge ocean of disappointment).
OK, but that's why we have an Xbox controller! A bad port won't scare us, right? NOPE. You connect the controller, start the game again, and the tool tips are still showing pictures of keyboard keys! So now not only are you trying to play a shooter with a controller (ugh), you're also guessing which button they mean when they show you some letter!
Now, you're thinking, sure, apparently there are some issues with the controls, but you can get used to anything as long as the story is good! This is some cross between The Matrix and Mass Effect or something! Again, NOPE. Story is flat, dialogue is clichéd, team mates are annoying.
But maybe it's a good shooter! Triple-NOPE. It's a cover-based, health-regenerating heap of boredom. The enemy AI is stupid, your team mate's AI is stupid, and the contrast with the game's backstory of human-like, super-intelligent AI, is almost funny.
The only redeeming quality of this game is the voice recognition mechanics. Haha, just kidding, it mostly doesn't work - but even if it did, it's totally gimmicky.
Now, the graphics is actually good - or at least on a standard level for a shooter. But this is basically
only thing that is normal in this game.
I don't usually write reviews, especially bad reviews ("if you can't say anything good, better say nothing"), but you, dear reader, deserve to be warned.

"Gears of War" with robots?
----
+ Good graphics
+ Robots take locational damage, i.e. you can blow off limbs and they adjust and keep coming for you.
+ Cool looking bosses
- Story has promise but isn't delivered well
- Keyboard and mouse controls are awful
- Tons of aim punch
- Voice recognition only works about 30% of the time
- Enemies will damage you regardless of you being in cover a lot of the time
- Terrible squad AI
- Flawed trust system
- The dialogue is 11 out of 10 for cliché nonsense, and not in a good way
- One character in the entire game is actually likeable (the french one)
----
When it comes down to choosing whether to recommend Binary Domain or not, I started thinking about what your time is worth. If you have limited time to game I would recommend you avoid this like the plague. And if you have a lot of time to try out a variety of games, I would say read the following rant in which I fail miserably to retain objectivity and then decide for yourself if you can tolerate the bad to dig out the good.
In summary though, Binary Domain is a game that promises a good time and fails to deliver (spectacularly) on almost every account.
----
The ranting begins;
I'll start with the parts I liked. The idea of being able to blow off the legs of a robot only to have it keep crawling menacingly towards you is great! You can shoot off a robot's gun wielding arm and it will bend over, pick up the gun with it's other hand and carry on. This is awesome. I also enjoyed one of the squad members (the french one), and one or two of the cutscenes in the game were well put together (shame about the others).
Unfortunately, the rest of the game is awful.
Firstly, keyboard and mouse controls just don't work properly. There is constant, unalterable mouse acceleration, and keyboard movement makes your character stutter wildly as he swaps from full lock in one animation to full lock in the opposite one without the gradual change you would get from using a joystick on a gamepad. These combine to make it extremely nauseating to play (and impossible to aim) - so I swapped to my gamepad.
Regardless of the control scheme you use, the aim punch (when you get hit your aim gets thrown wildly in a random direction) coupled with the laser accuracy of the enemies that will shoot you even behind cover in a lot of situations means that trying to play conservatively and aim at things like you would expect from a third person cover shooter just doesn't work - so I switched up my strategy and started to just charge at everything spraying madly from the hip.
The game uses your microphone and voice recognition software so that you can give your squad mates orders or respond to them in conversation with your voice. For me this worked fine if all I had to say was "yeah" over and over again, but it was a regular occurance in trying to say anything else for the game to get it wrong and all hell would break loose with my squad mates reputation scores - so finally, towards the end of the game, I figured out how to turn it off and use button inputs for all that instead.
The story itself has the seeds of being a good one - transhumanism, corporate espionage and governmental power abuse - but it does not deliver. The characters are petty and cliché and a majority of the cutscenes (with a few good exceptions) are rage inducing failures in attempted cinema. This is definately not "so bad it's good" territory. Just "so bad".
The game operates with a trust system for your allies that directly affects the course of the game. The AI seems to really love charging straight through your line of fire at every opportunity and then complaining at you - that is of course when the AI isn't just sitting in cover doing nothing for most of the game. You can give the AI the order to "charge!" or "fire!" in order to change this, but I found that often times charging got them killed and they acknowledged my fire order only to continue sitting in cover doing nothing. You can see by now how the problems are piling up, I hope.
Some more issues I encountered were;
- Main character is a complete tool. Supporting characters aren't much better.
- Whilst in cover you often end up with an ankle or an elbow sticking out which enemies will target mercilessly, making cover mostly useless.
- Unnecessary, clunky gun upgrade system (your teammates don't contribute much at all and your gun starts off complete garbage and eventually gets ridiculously overpowered).
- Selection of completely garbage-tier secondary weapons (The sniper rifle is useful at one or two points in the game only, the other machine guns/assault rifles aren't as good as your default one that you're forced to keep and which is as bland as it gets).
- No explanation or introduction to nanomachines (the means by which you upgrade your characters) at all. You could easily go the whole game without knowing they exist.
- Bosses in general look cool, but are frustrating rather than rewarding to beat. One example is a giant chandelier with tentacles that you fight in a tall circular room. You can either shoot an entire clip into it to spin it, gaining access to it's weak point, or run around the ring of the room to do the same. As soon as you do either, it just rotates its weak point to another side.
- One boss in particular took about 40 minutes to kill due to obscure weak point mechanics and invulnerability otherwise.
- There is a scene where you run over a collapsing bridge that looks cool but is executed completely awfully. You have to stop sprinting at multiple points (crushing the sense of momentum and urgency due to the drastic change in speed this involves) or fall because you're apparently incapable of hopping a small gap (with the worst falling animation i've possibly ever seen, I might add).
For me (as you might be able to tell from this rant), this game was super FRUSTRATING from start to finish.
Objectively though, is there anything of merit to this game that is worth the garbage controls and the litany of wonky stuff, especially when the market is saturated with great modern games in all kinds of genres these days?
Well the bosses *look* cool and robots responding to locational damage is nice, but other than that it's the very definition of "mediocre" and "failure to deliver" and as such absolutely not worth your time.

This is a thoroughly average game and, even at the reduced price I paid (around $5), I don't recommend buying it. It takes around 7 hours to finish and there are better ways to spend your 7 hours.
The core gameplay is okay but not stellar enough to overcome problems with pacing, dialogue, and the uselessness of your squad.
On paper, the game has a lot going for it. A voice-recognition system that means you can "talk" to your AI squadmates. Those "conversations" affect their morale which makes them more or less likely to follow your commands in the heat of combat. Sounds pretty nifty, right? The problems start almost immediately.
It isn't clear what choices the system accepts. Eventually you press TAB and see what the three pre-approved options are. None of are recognised when you say them, so you go into voice calibration settings. After five minutes you decide that the voice recognition is never going to work reliably for you. (For some reason I could never figure out how to say "Charge" in a way that the system would recognise....and I was born and raised in California with one of the blandest accents possible.)
When you turn off voice recognition you realise you're not missing much anyway. There's always one clear "good" choice (i.e. "don't be an ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, this is what a normal person would say") and there's no incentive for picking any other choice anyway. To make matter worse, it doesn't matter whether your teammates follow orders or not—they are so terrible in combat that you'll do all the work anyway. After the initial novelty wore off, I didn't give my teammates a single order in the last 5 hours of game play.
As I said, the gameplay is acceptable—though you "upgrade" your main weapon which means you don't get a lot of weapon variety through the course of the game, since your starting weapon is always better than any other option. But the real failing is the dialogue and pacing of the plot.
There is a ton of cringe-worthy dialogue, including a fair amount of some of recent gaming's worst casual sexism. The dialogue is possibly the worst I've seen in the last year or two.
The overall plot is reasonable but the pacing felt off. You spend 75% of the game breaking into the enemy base. The plot doesn't advance in any way whatsoever during these hours. It is purely, shoot, kill, advance to next checkpoint. Then you're suddenly in the enemy base and the plot goes from 0-60 in nothing flat. Then it is all over. The "plot" part of this game is entirely contained in the final two chapters which will take you about 2 hours to play through.
The characters and developments between them are strictly paint-by-numbers stereotypes. Two women are introduced. One is hot. So she's definitely the one who will become a love interest (in ~5 hours of real world time). The squad all seem to hate robots. For some reason that is never very clear. After less than an hour with the robot Caine they're all, "Having you around is sooooo useful! You totally saved us!" Duh. Robots are useful.
They clearly set this up for a sequel, which looks unlikely to be made at this point, if you're one of those people that hate any loose ends.
I didn't hate the game. But it was decidedly average and when we have so many great games to choose from, you can probably do better than this.

So basically you pay less than 5€ for the game itself. And it's definitely worth it!
The names you get, the persons, how they look, what you can use as a weapon and all the funny moments (watch the kinda epic trailer) make the game pretty damn solid.
The bots can be configured to play with you, although they are quite stupid. But watching them getting caught by the officers trying to commit a murder is somehow entertaining.

After all, you are not dependant on the developers to play the game in multiplayer, so catch it when it is on sale or share the price with your friends... Recommended!

I had initial downloaded this from an unnamed website several times to try out, having hear so many positive things about it.  However, each time I played for all of 5 minutes and uninstalled.  It looked like a cool, creepy concept that I would enjoy, therefore I kept it in my wishlist on Steam.  The reviews on Steam all say how great it is, so I figured if nothing else I should buy it at least to give the developers money since I had tried it previously and I'd like to think that many people can't be horribly wrong.
I decided to give it a solid try and I'm every glad I did.  It's a very enjoyable walking simulator (I guess it is?), with various paths/decisions you can choose.  Typically I'm put off by the Unity engine as most devolpers use it for it's simplicity and make terrible games with it.  Not this developer.  This is the best use of Unity I have ever seen (I don't count Hearthstone as Blizzard is not in the same league).  The graphics look amazing and the the transitional effects are very trippy.  I found the voice acting to fine, not great, but certainly did not take away from the game.
The only bug I encountered is a known issue in the Nursery Room at the end in Chapter 6.  Everytime I entered the screen started spinning, honestly I assumed it was a game mechanice for the carosel, however, upon reading in the forums on Steam, it's a glitch likely between Unity and the physics engine.  Not to worry, it's easily fixed, just hit Escape on the keyboard, fixed it instantly.  So definitely not game breaking in the least bit.
I took my time going through all the rooms I could, doing achievement, etc. and found it to be worth the price.  I still have to play the DLC I'll be doing that very soon (already purchased).  Anyone who has enjoyed What Remains Of Edith Finch, Firewatch, or The Vanishing Of Ethan Carter will enjoy this for sure, but I found it to be darker than any of them.  If you are unsure of purchasing wait for a sale, the sale price for the Masterpiece Edition is very affordable.
Overall, a great game with an enjoyable story/environment.  Graphics and paintings are top-notch!

I love
. I've played probably around 300 hours of it and there's still lots of unique quests to explore. That being said, if I take off my nostalgia glasses, there are some pretty major flaws that I feel anyone playing it for the first time today should be aware of. Breaking it down:
Cons:
* Combat of all types is boring. Magic/Stealth/Archery/Melee are all essentially reduced to keep-clicking-until-it-dies. On the magic side of things, the spell creation system is fun and there are lots of neat base spells to choose from, but in essence the combat itself is overly simple.
* The leveling system functions fine if you just don't pay attention to it, but optimal leveling is a tedious chore. If you are the type who just can't pass up an opportunity for maximum stat gains, this might be a big detractor.
* The dialogue is text based and most NPCs are just walking lore encyclopedias. The persuasion and bartering systems are laughably simple, and again, boring.
* The graphics haven't aged well, though it does have a strong artistic concept at its core.
* The menu interface is sub-par, but gets the job done.
Pros:
* Exploration is really well rewarded. Everywhere you look there's some small detail that hints at a story, or a unique artifact with interesting properties. Many of the ruins have secret entrances and places that you could easily miss.
*
does a good job of making you feel like your actions have impact. It could be better, but it is satisfying when factions will hate or love you depending on what you've done, and there are many unique dialog lines based on how famous you are.
* The quests are unique. Sure some of them blend together a little bit, but overall they are NOT just cookie-cutter quests. Most of them give you some insight into the world and how it works, or have some neat little twist.
* You can fly. It seems so trivial but I keep coming back to this as an example of the game's overwhelming freedom. It's fun scrounging around in the early game for limited-use levitation spells or the infamous Scrolls of Icarian Flight which make you jump so high you'll certainly die on your way back down. You start out so weak but there are powerful scrolls and spells to exploit that can change the entire game... the wild variance in the power of the enemies and items you encounter is one of
's stronger points.
* A final important pro is the modding community. If there are things you don't like about this game, chances are high there's a mod that can change it. In particular, I have a had good luck with graphics mod compilations and just general expansion packs. Of course, modding is not necessarily everyone's cup of tea.
In summary, this game has many great features and in some ways the sense of depth and scale you get when immersed in it is unrivaled by any game since. However, it requires a certain type of gamer, (or a certain amount of modding,) to get past its unpalatable quirks and into the wonderful world beneath.

This review will be a bit lengthy, please bear with me. I wanted to be as thorough and fair as I could possibly be regarding this game and how EXTREMELY FUN it was to play.
I came to the Steam community originally to play Jet Set Radio on my computer. While browsing the games here, I came across the game "HuniePop" by using the filters "Mature" and "Nudity" :) .
I watched the trailer for HuniePop and quickly became interested as I've always enjoyed dating-sim games since the early days of Newgrounds and SimGirls. To compare this game to Candy Crush Saga or any other match-3 games would be doing this game a great disservice. HuniePop is not only an detailed and challenging puzzle game, but by far one of the best dating sims I've EVER played.
The gameplay is smooth as silk, the music is cool and quirky, the voice acting is INCREDIBLE and the artwork is STELLAR - all of these aspects work together to pull you into the game's world of fun, romance, sex and seduction. When first I started playing HuniePop, I had no idea how addicting it would be - until I was running late for work after playing the game for 12 hours straight. Getting to know the girls and all of their details was a truly rewarding experience - I literally had a pen and a paper writing down each one's birthday, weight, favorite color, etc.
Even more fulfilling was how MODERN HuniePop is, utilizing dialogue and slang of today's society. I literally laughed out loud when I unlocked Audrey's "Thottie" outfit - saying to myself "Wait, what? Did that really just say 'Thottie'?" Audrey is a great example of your run-of-the-mill valley girl that is ♥♥♥♥♥y, edgy and likes to party. Kyu is a real cut-up too, treating you like a sexy and spunky mentor while kickin' it with you like one of the bros. Tiffany is a cute bookworm that will fulfill all of your anime schoolgirl needs. Aiko is the sexy and kinky teacher who likes to chill and gamble. Kyanna (my favorite) is a great example of your modern day mom who likes to have fun here and there, but wants to work on herself and enjoy life. Lola is a cute stewardess who is competitive at sports and travels a lot. Nikki is the cute, shy gamer chick who's a tad bit emo but sweet. Jessie is the cougar mom who feeds off of alcohol and sex and Beli is the spiritual yoga girl who likes to take things slow.
After you beat the game by obtaining the panties of all 9 girls (Kyu included), the game becomes extended with the introduction and discovery of 3 additional girls. The replay value is also enhanced with an unlockable Alpha Mode (harder difficulty, endless gameplay) which allows you to collect whatever collectibles you might have missed during the story playthrough. The ability to customize the hairstyle and outfit of each character is a plus as well, another cool option to an already diverse and entertaining game. The idea of unlocking sexy artwork after every successful date is genius as well; cute little photo attachments to messages sent to your HunieBee. Another cool aspect to the dating mode in HuniePop is the "dating gifts" and how they correlate to the puzzle and it's progression.
Overall, I really enjoyed playing HuniePop. It's a game I would recommend to puzzle-game nerds as well as anime aficionados. Actually, I would recommend it to any one who just wants to have a good time playing a game and enjoying a comedic, light-hearted and sexy experience. I even introduced the game to my wife (who loves puzzle games) and she loves it. We've spent the last few nights playing the game together over a few glasses of wine when the little one is asleep.
HuniePop is an extremely entertaining game that I truly enjoyed playing.

Performance seems to have sorted itself out in recent updates; Good news!
Pros:
- Constant updates (Good to see devs actively working on the game)
- Base building mechanics
- Looting
- F2P
- Weapon balance constantly being checked/reworked to be more fair
- Damage indicators (Very useful!)
Cons:
- Poor weapon balancing (Though it's constantly being tweaked to be more balanced)
- Mediocre gunplay (A little jank, could be better)
- Pay to win, literally
- Few base-building options currently
- Limited basebuilding control (Rotations locked at 10 degree increments, no snapping of any kind, no height adjustment of any kind; sort of ties in with previous point)
- Fairly poor hit-reg
- Early Access/Alpha
In recent time, the devs have put out several updates and seem to be paying close attention to the balancing of the game and are actively trying to make it better/more fair, which is good.
The pay to win aspect is still very much a thing in the context that certain paid for classes have access to weapons/equipment otherwise completely unavailable to F2Players except by looting the body of a P2W player. Either that or have much easier access to otherwise slightly rare/valuable equipment (Rockets, TNT, High-quality healing items, copious amounts of ammo)
This probably wouldn't be such an issue if it weren't for the fact that one player could just keep respawning at no cost to themselves or their team and supply everyone with high-quality gear and thousands of rounds of ammo to boot. Though I suppose that's
a good thing, but clearly game breaking; Could easily be remedied with a suicide/respawn cooldown.
On the subject of gunplay/hit-reg; It almost feels like the game flips a coin every time your bullet connects with an enemy, because I swear only half of my bullets actually deal damage. Although it probably doesn't help much that most of the actual gunplay is just super clunky in general. Aiming down sights (with the exception of proper scoped weapons) almost seems like it makes you less accurate. Probably not true, though I've not done any actual tests myself. The shooting mechanics very heavily support the B-Hop Spray 'N Pray method, with the exception of sniper rifles at range, though even then it still sort of applies. Meaning just about any automatic will almost always beat out any semi-auto or bolt-action, which I suppose sort of makes sense? But trust me when I say it's not exactly for the reasons one might expect due to the general balancing of the weapons.
On a completely subjective & unrelated note of suggestions for possible improvements;
- Character customization
- Respawn/Suicide timer (As mentioned above)
- More Loot!
- Better collision detection (Just for everything, Players, Buildings, Vehicles, etc.)
- Rebalance all the things! (Doesn't really need to be said 'cuz I already know they're going to be rebalancing all over the place anyway)
Bottom line;
It functions, it's free, it doesn't take up a lot of space, has potential, and is contantly being worked on. All good signs, could end up being a really tight game in due time, but for now I think most people would just get quickly frustrated/bored with this game in its current state, and for various reasons.

In normal gameplay without mods, progressing and getting fame, right to rule, etc can take ages. A single game progressing from lowest to top tier could take easily 100+ hours. Much of that time would be grinding battles or repeating medial tasks.
This is made even worse with improving relations with people, which often involve doing the same tasks over and over giving the same responses. The game becomes incredibly tedious. Being stuck in the same place you were 20 hours ago becomes really unfun to me, though some people won't mind.
Still, that issue is fixable, so I give the game a full reccomendation. It's awesome fun seeing 200 man battles of soldiers all fighting at once.
