Layers of Fear is a first person horror game which is, surprisingly, better than most of the bulk, blase fluff that you typically find in the horror category.
The story starts off simple: You play as a painter who is suffering from a creator's block and whose ultimate goal is to finish his magnum opus, his final painting. To do so, the painter must collect certain items around his home mansion. What starts off simply soon turns into a living nightmare as the painter descents into a state of psychosis while wandering aimlessly inside his mansion. Ghastly visions filled with past trauma and human mistakes begin to creep in. Long-repressed feelings of anger, sadness, and guilt take the form of menacing and sometimes creepy imagery which jumps at you when you least expect it.
You have no way of defending yourself, and hiding is not mandatory. Layers of Fear shows a lot of promise, but falls flat on the midway point after it becomes clear that the horrors pose no real threat to you. As you can't really "die" and failure has no consequence, this haunted house simulator loses much of its charm. There is only one way, a really scripted pipe which one must go through. Scattered about are mementos which reveal information of the story behind the scenes and the painter's sordid past. There are also some light puzzles, but these are not particularly fun or interesting and serve only as fluff to make the game seem more long. My playthrough took me roughly 2,5 hours. This is a short stint into the world of horror for the normal asking price of 20€.
Technically the game is stunning. You can open most of the cabinets, chests, and doors in the mansion. The spooky effects on the environment look great, and there are no technical hiccups to speak of. Audio is all-around spectacular, as well.
Layers of Fear is an above average first person horror game with all bark and no bite. What starts on a high note, ends with a wimper since the game stops being really "scary" at the midway point.
Pros:
+ Technically stunning
+ Great atmosphere...
Con:
- ...which is diluted by the lack of no real threat from the horrors which lurk about
- No replay value after completion
- A rather steep price (normal price 20€)
Layers of Fear is not a bad purchase if you can get at a discount during a sale.

I played the game not thinking I was going to like it, but I was drawn into it from nearly the beginning. The story may start slowly, but soon it will suck you into a swirling tornado of madness as you learn about the life of your character, a painter, and how he got to the point he is at in his life. This slide into insanity is perfectly encapsulated in a graphical mind bending world that changes and flips on you at any moment. You were walking down a hall chasing a child and turn a corner and suddenly your back where you started and the kid runs by you again. You come to a locked door and turn around and you are suddenly in a different room. You enter an office and suddenly the entire room starts literally warping skyward in front of you. There are a ton of small and large ways this game tries to break your mind, and I enjoyed every single one of them.
The story twists as much as the graphics as you learn what it was that drove this painter mad. Yes, it can sag a bit from time to time, but it is an absolutely fantastic nightmare I would live again and again. Couldn't recommend enough!

Blood of the Werewolf tries to be an old school platformer, but fails to capture that sense of fun and challenge. It's a very difficult platformer (due to the poor controls and hit boxes) that has a few main features that make the game frustrating and a chore to play. The biggest of these is the checkpoint system. Checkpoints are too few and far between. If we compare this to Super Meat Boy, it would be like playing through 3-5 levels without a place to continue from. This problem further persists into the Boss fights. A boss fight can take upwards of 8-10 minutes, and one boss fight has multiple stages with no checkpoints in between these stages/new health bars.
Coupled with the knockback, and repetitive platforming sections (some sections are an actual copy paste, but with more fireballs, more fireball directions, or spikes which instantly kill you). It doesn't feel good to complete these sections, it feels like a chore since they're usually way too long. There are also issues where the foreground hides objects that you need to dodge or be aware of, which is just frustrating. There are a lot of good platformers out there, but with levels that take upwards of 20 minutes to complete, a poor checkpoint system, and frankly tedious boss fights (seriously, NO ONE wants to fight a boss for over 8 minutes, that's worse than some MMOs!) I can't recommend Blood of the Werewolf even though I love platformers. I bought it on sale, and I feel like I got my moneys worth in play time, but it wasn't enjoyable and I would glady have my time back, they can keep my money. I kept hoping it would get better, and it didn't.

I got this really cheap and well I guess that pretty much made it worth buying it. The art style is quite nice and the boss levels I played (Creature and Hyde) seemed quite nice even if simple. However as far as the general levels design goes I find it a bit weak. They might seem hard but in truth I found myself dying over and over due to silly enemies combos that are pretty hard to avoid without any previous knowledge. The way I see it a perfect level design for platformers should be hard, engaging and fluid. Blood of the Werewolf fails in the last two. Music and voice acting sounded ok.
You're given some powers however from what I played they're barely used/integrated with the level design. They're all pretty much just things to kill quite resistant sack of meat. Which is quite sad since I enjoyed the way they worked, even though most of the time they were useless... And once again we go back to bad level design or at least identity. There's a timer and yet you're given a long range bow that takes forever to kill anything...
As for the story, I tried checking a quick cutscenes video on youtube but there's none (guess I should find a playthrough). Also the videos on the gamefolder only show the animated sequences and lack the text part which seem to contain most of the story. From what I gathered the setting is pretty straighforward: You're a baddass mother (which I really liked!) looking to find who kidnaped your son. From the Trial version you know it's Dr. Frakenstein and he's responsible for sending out the monster bosses to delay you for his experiments with your son.
.

In conclusion, gameplay is generally weak. Boss fights are nice although simple. Music and voice acting sounded ok. The setting seems reasonable but the story seems short and weak (but it is a short game)  with an endind that doesn't really seem to reward you barely manages to pull you for the sequel(?). So if you're looking into buying this game I guess I wouldn't recommend it. Sure I grabbed it for cheap and if you're curious might as well try it out. However there's not enough good thing on it to recommend it over other titles. Even though the art style looks nice and the setting is pretty cool :)
